This means that for the Philippines readiness for war won’t come about until after 10 years. Such must be true, particularly for the US, which calls the ultimate shots.

What do all the above indicate?

That the US won’t be ready to war with China until after 10 years.

And yet for the US, such is unthinkable.

*   ![Image 2: Duterte’s tax records need audit – BIR exec](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253725.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Duterte’s tax records need audit – BIR exec](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/news/dutertes-tax-records-need-audit-bir-exec/2442826)

The US is deeply in mess with Iran in the Middle East, and there are no indications that it will get out of the trouble in the short run. It direly needs the billions of dollars ready for the taking from Taiwan through their pending arms deal. The only kink hampering that deal is the objection of China. This is to be expected since against who else would Taiwan use those arms but China?

So, no way for the US to get its arms deal with Taiwan done but by forcing it through China.

And that means war, not in the far future but now.

Why then, as Teodoro consistently indicates, make preparations for war that is yet long to come?

*   ![Image 3: Man arrested after breaching NAIA security to reunite with OFW wife](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252636.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Man arrested after breaching NAIA security to reunite with OFW wife](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/news/man-arrested-after-breaching-naia-security-to-reunite-with-ofw-wife/2442354)

Well, Teodoro has not been appointed to the post of defense secretary twice for nothing.

That he stays in that post only proves he is in the good graces with the real appointing power in the security sector — America.

Everything he does is for the betterment of the US position in its antagonism with China.

Making America appear weak, when in fact it is strong, not ready for war when in fact it can deliver the effective strike anytime it so wishes.

Teodoro has been the effective decoy for America’s real war readiness.

To this column, Teodoro’s moves bring back memories of Operation Overlord, the code name for the covert Allied strategy of retaking France from Nazi occupation in World War II.

All indications were that the allies landing would be at Pas-de-Calais, the nearest point in France across the English Channel. Among the many ploys employed by the allies aside from visible troops and facilities deployment were radio messages deliberately meant for Nazi interception and always identifying Pas-de-Calais as the site of the Allied landing.

Accordingly, all Nazi preparations were geared for the defense of Pas-de-Calais.

But then comes June 6, 1944, the real D-Day. Thousands of Allied paratroopers drop — not at Pas-de-Calais but in Normandy, which turns out to be the real site for the retaking of France, without any Nazi resistance.

From that point onward, the Nazi forces were on retreat back to Germany, culminating in ultimate surrender.

The point being driven here is that Teodoro’s obviously intended media splurge is a decoy for drawing attention away from what is already a US readiness to war with China now.

The recent visit of President Xi Jinping to Washington betrayed a desperation on China’s end to pursue what still could be achieved diplomatically in averting the ultimate catastrophe that could result from a final outburst of the Taiwan flash point. President Trump’s body language betrayed that he was not listening but was sticking to a resolve earlier already reached on the issue.

Notice how Trump was inwardly squeamish from some private shenanigan he was nursing inside while Xi was making a last-ditch attempt to convince him of his oft-repeated imploration that both the US and China would gain from cooperation but lose from confrontation.

But the smirk on Trump’s face betrayed he was actually into one more Operation Overlord.

As Sun Tzu puts it: “Make your plans be as dark as night. And when you move, strike like thunder.”

title: The banana chip witch hunt: China, CALE88 and the weaponization of national security against Sara Duterte
summary: APPARENTLY, in the Philippines today, even banana chips can become a national security threat — provided the buyer is Chinese and the company selling them has a connection to the Duterte family. Welcome to the latest spectacle in Philippine
content:
APPARENTLY, in the Philippines today, even banana chips can become a national security threat — provided the buyer is Chinese and the company selling them has a connection to the Duterte family.

Welcome to the latest spectacle in Philippine politics, where ordinary commercial transactions become geopolitical intrigue, Chinese corporate ownership becomes a convenient insinuation of foreign interference, and allegations appear as established facts long before the evidence catches up.

At the center of this controversy is CALE88 Foods Corp., a Philippine company previously associated with lawyer Manases “Mans” Carpio, the husband of Vice President Sara Duterte. In the ongoing impeachment trial against the VP, Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) records fueled sensational headlines alleging that approximately P319.33 million flowed from China and Hong Kong into CALE88.

The insinuation and narrative from the current political establishment in the Philippines under a Marcos Jr. government were hardly subtle: The headline claimed that Sara Duterte secretly received financing from Beijing. How inventive!

But an explosive allegation is not necessarily a substantiated one. This controversy illustrates how easily legitimate financial scrutiny can become entangled with political rivalry, strategic suspicion and the increasingly fashionable habit of finding Chinese interference wherever the words China and Chinese exist.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

The crucial distinction is simple: Money received by a Philippine company from Chinese commercial counterparties is not automatically money from the Chinese government. Neither is corporate revenue automatically money personally received by the vice president. Yet somewhere between the financial records and the political headlines, these distinctions appear to have become inconvenient and blurred.

AMLC executive director Ronel Buenaventura testified clearly that AMLC has no records whatsoever showing that China, as a country, or its government, funneled funds to CALE88. It is on record in the impeachment trial proceedings. When asked whether the AMLC had records identifying how much of CALE88’s transactions benefited the vice president or her husband, he said there were none. Hence, the most politically incendiary accusation against the vice president is unproven.

**From banana chips to China’s alleged political financing**

What makes this controversy particularly revealing is the Oct. 6 Bilyonaryo news channel report, which cites Bureau of Customs records showing that CALE88 exported about P217.3 million worth of products to China, out of P246.6 million in total exports since 2023. Its buyers included 13 Chinese companies, among them Beijing Zhenweifang Food Co. and China National Township Enterprises.

Now, here is a revolutionary lesson in Economics 101 that Gilberto “Gibo” Teodoro Jr. and Antonio Trillanes IV might wish to revisit: When a Philippine company exports products to China, Chinese buyers are expected to pay for them, right? Shocking, isn’t it?

But since when does legitimate international trade automatically become clandestine political financing? Does selling banana chips to Chinese companies now constitute foreign interference or treason?

These documented exports fundamentally challenge the insinuation that Chinese remittances necessarily represent political funding. If the prosecution suspects otherwise, produce the invoices, trace the money, identify the beneficiaries and prove the illicit purpose. Commercial exports do not automatically validate every remittance, but neither does a Chinese buyer establish wrongdoing.

Evidence, not geopolitical paranoia and sinophobia. Pointing toward Beijing and shouting “Aha!” is not proof. It is political theater masquerading as investigation.

**Hontiveros insinuations and her usual anti-China antics**

Sen. Risa Hontiveros has raised concerns over CALE88’s transactions with Chinese companies allegedly linked to state-owned enterprises and the Chinese Communist Party, including China National Township Enterprises and firms connected to Xinjiang Fruit Industry Group.

Question: Since when did trading with Chinese state-owned enterprises become evidence of foreign interference?

China’s state-owned enterprises are deeply integrated into its domestic economy and international trade. They operate in agriculture, energy, logistics, infrastructure, manufacturing and numerous other industries. That is hardly a state secret. That is hardly a geopolitical revelation.

Does purchasing agricultural products from a Chinese state-owned enterprise automatically constitute foreign interference? Does selling banana chips to a state-linked company make a Filipino entrepreneur an agent of Beijing? By that absurd logic, would this mean that countless Philippine companies doing business with Chinese state enterprises should be investigated as potential national-security threats?

Hontiveros has every right to scrutinize questionable transactions. But Chinese state ownership is not proof of clandestine political financing, much less evidence that Sara Duterte personally received funds from Beijing. Hontiveros should stop confusing commercial relationships with political conspiracy. Otherwise, this becomes guilt by association, dressed up as national security scrutiny.

**Gibo inserted himself again!**

Defense Secretary Gibo Teodoro warned that allegations of Chinese financing, if substantiated, could have serious national-security implications. Fair enough. But since when should the country’s defense establishment amplify geopolitical suspicion before establishing the facts/evidence?

Where is the evidence of a national-security violation? Was classified information compromised? Was there an agreement to influence Philippine foreign policy? Were illegal political contributions made? Did Beijing issue instructions to Sara Duterte? Any proof of this?

Where is the proof, Gibo? Or are we substituting geopolitical paranoia, imagination and insinuation for hard evidence now?

A defense secretary, of all people, should understand that national security is far too serious to be reduced to political theater, speculation, imagination, hallucination or sinophobia.

Simply invoking China does not magically transform a commercial transaction into espionage, foreign interference or treason. National security demands credible, factual, evidence-based intelligence assessment, not geopolitical hallucinations and bigotry masquerading as intelligence.

**Conclusion**

What Filipinos deserve is accountability, not political theater. AMLC testimony reportedly identified P1.25 billion in aggregate covered and suspicious transactions involving CALE88 between 2022 and 2025. These warrant an investigation. The defense must explain the financial discrepancies, while the prosecution must establish wrongdoing through credible, verifiable evidence.

But investigating questionable corporate transactions is one thing; accusing Vice President Sara Duterte of secretly receiving Chinese government funding is quite another. The latter requires compelling evidence, not political insinuations, sensational headlines or national-security rhetoric. The burden of proof cannot be replaced by geopolitical paranoia or sinophobia.

More troubling is the political climate under the Marcos Jr. administration, where almost anything associated with China increasingly invites suspicion and allegations of sinister intent. Such a mindset risks discouraging legitimate investment, distorting commercial realities and undermining an independent Philippine foreign policy. Nationalism/patriotism should never require compulsory hostility toward China.

The CALE88 controversy involves documented exports, substantial financial transactions requiring reconciliation and corporate relationships deserving examination. What is unproven is the sensational allegation that Beijing secretly financed Sara Duterte.

And here lies the spectacular absurdity of Philippine politics: Marcos Jr.’s government is grappling with allegations of massive corruption, food and energy insecurity, economic uncertainty, strategic dependence and overwhelming American influence, yet somehow finding time to turn banana chips into an international conspiracy! What the hell!?

The greatest irony? While billions in public funds face scrutiny over questionable government flood control and infrastructure projects, some politicians seem remarkably eager to find treason in banana-chip shipments.

That is hardly a serious national security analysis. It is political theater seasoned with geopolitical paranoia and a generous helping of sinophobia. And frankly, the Filipino people deserve far better.

title: Effect of minor discrepancies between testimony in court and affidavit of the complainant
summary: _**Dear PAO,**_ _**I am accused of a certain crime, and the complainant made minor discrepancies between her affidavit and her testimony in court. Am I correct in my assumption that such discrepancies would affect her credibility?**_ _**Kum
content:
_**Dear PAO,**_

_**I am accused of a certain crime, and the complainant made minor discrepancies between her affidavit and her testimony in court. Am I correct in my assumption that such discrepancies would affect her credibility?**_

_**Kumpormae**_

*   [Can overtime work be used to offset an employee’s absence?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/06/legal-advice/can-overtime-work-be-used-to-offset-an-employees-absence/2439267)

**Dear Kumpormae,**

Generally speaking, the qualification of a witness, such as the complainant, is provided under Section 21, Rule 130 of A.M. No. 19-08-15-SC, or the 2019 Revised Rules on Evidence, which reads:

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

“All persons who can perceive, and perceiving, can make known their perception to others, may be witnesses.”

Correlative thereto, Section 22 of the said Rules also provides that:

“A witness can testify only to those facts which he or she knows of his or her personal knowledge; that is, which are derived from his or her own perception.”

*   ![Image 1: Duterte’s tax records need audit – BIR exec](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253725.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Duterte’s tax records need audit – BIR exec](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/news/dutertes-tax-records-need-audit-bir-exec/2442826)

The examination of a witness is to be done in open court. This is in consonance with Section 1, Rule 132 of the same Rules:

“The examination of witnesses presented in a trial or hearing shall be done in open court, and under oath or affirmation. Unless the witness is incapacitated to speak, or the question calls for a different mode of answer, the answers of the witness shall be given orally.”

It may happen that there will be inconsistencies between the testimony in court and the earlier affidavit of the complainant or witness. With respect to minor inconsistencies, the pronouncement of the Supreme Court in Pacu-an vs. People of the Philippines, G.R. No. 237542, June 16, 2021, penned by Honorable Associate Justice Edgardo L. Delos Santos, is very enlightening, viz.:

_“Given the natural frailties of the human mind and its incapacity to assimilate all material details of a given incident, slight inconsistencies and variances in the declarations of a witness hardly weaken their probative value. It is well settled that immaterial and insignificant details do not discredit a testimony on the very material and significant point bearing on the very act of accused-appellants._

*   ![Image 2: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

_In Avelino v. People, the Court reiterated the ruling in Madali v. People and held that “[a]s long as the testimonies of the witnesses corroborate one another on material points, minor inconsistencies therein cannot destroy their credibility. Inconsistencies on minor details do not undermine the integrity of a prosecution witness.” In People v. Manigo, the Court ruled that as between a sworn statement or affidavit and an open court testimony, courts must always give more weight to the open court declarations since “affidavits being taken ex-parte are usually incomplete and inaccurate.” Furthermore, in People v. Dayaday, the Court ruled that sworn statements taken ex parte are, as a general rule, considered to be inferior to the testimony given in open court, to wit:_

_A sworn statement or an affidavit does not purport to contain a complete compendium of the details of the event narrated by the affiant. Sworn statements taken ex parte are generally considered to be inferior to the testimony given in open court.”_

Applying the above-quoted jurisprudence to your situation, minor discrepancies or inconsistencies between the testimony given in open court and the affidavit of the complainant does not discredit her or affect her credibility as long as the testimony can be corroborated in its material points. In fact, minor inconsistencies are even treated as badges of truth instead of an indication of falsehood because it shows that the same was not rehearsed or coached. As between the testimony and the affidavit, the former will be controlling because the complainant-witness was subjected to direct and cross examination.

We hope that we were able to answer your queries. This advice is solely based on the facts you have narrated and our appreciation of the same. Our opinion may vary when other facts are changed or elaborated.

title: Is governance a brake or a catalyst?
summary: A WELL-DESIGNED regulatory framework is often described as a “brake” on innovation. Too many rules slow companies down, too much compliance burdens entrepreneurs, and too much uncertainty chases away investment. But that framing is incomple
content:
A WELL-DESIGNED regulatory framework is often described as a “brake” on innovation. Too many rules slow companies down, too much compliance burdens entrepreneurs, and too much uncertainty chases away investment. But that framing is incomplete.

In the digital era, artificial intelligence (AI), data flows, online marketplaces and cybersecurity risks evolve at the speed of software releases. Here, governance must also be seen as a catalyst. It can create the conditions under which innovation becomes safer, faster and more widely shared. When regulation clarifies rights and responsibilities, levels the playing field and establishes trust, innovators can build on something stronger than their own risk models.

Public trust, in turn, enlarges adoption; adoption enlarges markets; markets attract more innovation. In that sense, regulatory frameworks are not merely constraints — they are infrastructure for digital economies.

*   [The banana chip witch hunt: China, CALE88 and the weaponization of national security against Sara Duterte](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/the-banana-chip-witch-hunt-china-cale88-and-the-weaponization-of-national-security-against-sara-duterte/2442743)

To make governance both a brake and a catalyst, regulators must master three skills. They must set clear baselines without freezing experimentation, build compliance pathways that are practical for companies of different sizes and enforce rules consistently enough that the marketplace believes they apply to everyone.

This is why “good regulation” cannot be only a legal text. It must also include standards, guidance, supervisory capacity and dispute resolution mechanisms. Otherwise, the rules remain aspirational — ineffective as protection and harmful as uncertainty.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

A regulatory framework promotes innovation when it reduces information asymmetry. Platforms often move faster than consumers, and consumers often cannot evaluate risks, especially in AI-driven systems where decisions are opaque. Regulations that demand transparency, independent audits for high-risk AI use, and clear consumer recourse systems give both innovators and users a shared understanding of how the digital market works. That shared understanding converts vague risk where investment can thrive.

At the same time, regulation strengthens trust by tackling the three trust deficits that repeatedly stall digital adoption: privacy insecurity, fraud and manipulation, and unequal power. Data protection laws, security standards and anti-fraud enforcement build confidence that digital services won’t exploit users. Rules for platform conduct include fair ranking practices, complaint handling and accountability for content harms. They signal that public interests matter, not only engagement metrics.

These ideas connect to the “digital majority” thesis. If digital technology reaches and empowers most people, then the legitimacy of the rules becomes essential. A digital majority cannot be governed by architecture alone. It also requires democratic accountability: regulations that reflect public values, not only corporate incentives. The emerging powers that increasingly design digital ecosystems — across Asia, Africa and Latin America — must therefore craft governance that supports innovation while guarding inclusion.

*   ![Image 1: US-China war now](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253555.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[US-China war now](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/opinion/columns/us-china-war-now/2442742)

**Asia: ‘Sandboxing’ and data governance**

In Asia, a recurring regulatory strategy for balancing innovation and trust is the use of regulatory sandboxes and phased compliance. Sandboxes let companies test products with temporary flexibility while regulators learn. That learning loop is the “catalyst” part: It turns enforcement into adaptation rather than surprise crackdowns later.

For instance, the Singapore approach — often referenced in fintech and digital service governance — has long used a risk-based framework that encourages experimentation while requiring safeguards around consumer protection, cybersecurity and compliance reporting. The result is not “no regulation,” but a structure where innovators know the boundaries early.

In South Korea, trust-building for digital markets is often tied to strong consumer protections and enforcement coordination across sectors. Meanwhile, Japan has frequently served as a regional reference point for institutionalizing governance practices relevant to digital technologies, combining regulatory clarity with emphasis on responsible media and public communication.

*   ![Image 2: Man arrested after breaching NAIA security to reunite with OFW wife](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252636.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Man arrested after breaching NAIA security to reunite with OFW wife](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/news/man-arrested-after-breaching-naia-security-to-reunite-with-ofw-wife/2442354)

Another major Asian theme is data governance. When data protection laws and cross-border transfer rules are comprehensible and predictable, firms can invest in compliance rather than fear sudden enforcement. Frameworks that specify roles help companies design systems correctly from the start. In emerging economies, this clarity is particularly valuable: It allows smaller startups to compete because rules are not applied arbitrarily.

Africa’s digital transformation — especially through mobile money, e-commerce and fintech — has shown how trust can become a competitive advantage. Where financial inclusion depends on digital systems, regulation becomes a direct driver of adoption.

Take mobile money. In many African markets, the speed of growth outpaced early rules. Later regulatory frameworks focused on licensing, interoperability, agent conduct, consumer protection and dispute resolution. When regulators required safeguards, they reduced the uncertainty that prevented mainstream users from trusting digital payments.

A concrete example is Kenya’s mobile money ecosystem. The country’s regulatory evolution demonstrated that payment innovation can scale rapidly when supervision and rules are tailored to real-world usage. Requirements around agent settlement practices, risk management and customer protections transformed mobile money from an experimental service into trusted infrastructure.

*   ![Image 3: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

That trust broadened the market — female users, rural users, small merchants and informal-sector workers included. This created a demand for additional fintech innovation such as credit scoring, savings products and digital merchant payments.

In Nigeria, the evolution of digital finance regulation illustrates another balance: promoting innovation while managing systemic risks. Financial regulators have periodically tightened and clarified licensing and compliance requirements to reduce fraud and increase system resilience. While such tightening can feel like a “brake” to startups, clearer licensing criteria and compliance guidance often become a “catalyst” over time by attracting more sustainable investment and reducing risk for legitimate players.

Latin America offers strong lessons on governance for digital trust in environments where inequality, misinformation risk and fraud are significant. Here, regulation often must protect consumers not only from product risks but also from market manipulation.

One area where trust and innovation collide is platform power. When a few platforms dominate distribution, market entry becomes harder. Regulatory frameworks that encourage competition can stimulate innovation by lowering “access barriers.”

Another lesson concerns consumer protection and data privacy. When users fear that personal data will be mishandled — or that digital services will not respond to complaints — adoption slows. Latin American regulators have increasingly focused on data protection implementation and enforcement to build consumer confidence. Where privacy rights are enforceable and institutions are capable, innovators can differentiate through trust rather than through opaque data practices.

Regulation also plays a vital role in managing misinformation and harmful online content. Yet here the “brake vs catalyst” balance is delicate: Heavy-handed approaches that undermine free expression can chill legitimate innovation in media, civic tech and journalism. The best models aim for procedural fairness, include clear standards for removal or restriction, transparency reports, avenues for appeal and platform obligations. They should be measurable rather than arbitrary.

A digital majority implies that digital systems are no longer peripheral; they are civic infrastructure. In that context, regulation is not an obstacle to progress — it becomes the condition for sustainable progress. When governance aligns innovation incentives with public values, it transforms trust into a multiplier. It reduces fraud, improves reliability, strengthens consumer rights and increases adoption. With more users and a more trusted environment, innovation accelerates and becomes more inclusive.

_Danton Remoto is writing a book on the digital majority. His literary books are being sold at Fully Booked, National Bookstore, Shopee, Lazada and Central Books website; Kinokuniya in Asia; and Amazon globally._

title: Chinese teacher recall sparks debate, concern
summary: ​RETIRED US Air Force Col. Ray Powell, director of maritime security initiative SeaLight, said that China has used travel and education warnings to pressure governments in diplomatic disputes. ​This comes as about 150 Chinese volunteer teac
content:
​RETIRED US Air Force Col. Ray Powell, director of maritime security initiative SeaLight, said that China has used travel and education warnings to pressure governments in diplomatic disputes.

​This comes as about 150 Chinese volunteer teachers were abruptly recalled from Philippine schools following security concerns and heightened scrutiny surrounding state-sponsored Chinese influence operations in the country.

​Geopolitical analyst Herman Tiu Laurel, president of the Asian Century Philippines Strategic Studies Institute, dismissed Powell’s allegations as speculative, saying the teachers’ parents sought their return out of concern for their children’s safety amid what he described as persistent anti-China media coverage.

*   [Robredo, Baste Duterte lead contrasting 2028 scenarios – survey](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/08/news/robredo-baste-duterte-lead-contrasting-2028-scenarios-survey/2441041)

The Federation of Filipino-Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry reportedly said the recall was approved by the organization and the Chinese Embassy in Manila following concerns raised by parents in China.

​The circumstances surrounding the decision, including who ordered the teachers’ return and when, remain unclear.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

​Powell said no teacher, family member, or specific threat had been publicly identified to substantiate claims that the educators were in danger.

​The Chinese Embassy has denounced what it called “malicious smear campaigns” and urged the Philippine government to protect the safety and legitimate rights and interests of Chinese nationals.

​Powell said his concerns centered on the institutions involved in training and deploying the teachers, rather than on the educators themselves.

*   ![Image 1: Man arrested after breaching NAIA security to reunite with OFW wife](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252636.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Man arrested after breaching NAIA security to reunite with OFW wife](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/news/man-arrested-after-breaching-naia-security-to-reunite-with-ofw-wife/2442354)

​He cited records showing that Jinan University trained 43 of the 56 Filipino students in the Philippine Chinese Education Research Center’s 2024 teacher-training cohort. The university describes itself as jointly established with the Chinese Communist Party’s Central Committee United Front Work Department.

​Powell noted that China’s volunteer-teacher position list for 2027, published around Sept. 22, contained no Philippine posts, compared with 45 positions for 2025 and 32 for 2026. He said this suggested the program might already have been undergoing a reduction before the recall became public.

​Laurel said the lack of clarity over who ordered the teachers’ return undermined the allegations against Beijing. He maintained that the decision followed appeals from concerned parents worried about what he described as persistent anti-China coverage in Philippine media.

​Powell cited previous disputes to support his argument that China uses travel warnings and restrictions to exert political pressure.

*   ![Image 2: Duterte’s tax records need audit – BIR exec](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1253725.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Duterte’s tax records need audit – BIR exec](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/news/dutertes-tax-records-need-audit-bir-exec/2442826)

​During the 2012 Bajo de Masinloc (Scarborough Shoal) standoff, China issued travel safety advice and Chinese travel agencies suspended tours to the Philippines. Chinese authorities also rejected Philippine banana shipments, citing quarantine concerns.

​He cited China’s restrictions on group tours to South Korea in 2017 following Seoul’s decision to deploy a US-made missile defense system, as well as disputes involving Australia, Turkey, Japan, and Palau.

​Laurel countered that travel advisories are not unique to China. He cited efforts by Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan to promote tourism to the Philippines and expand flights by Chinese airlines.

​He claimed Chinese tourist arrivals increased by 64 percent in 2026 but provided no supporting figures in his statement.

*   ![Image 3: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

​The reported recall has disrupted Mandarin instruction in some Manila schools, with affected students turning to substitute teachers and online classes.

​Powell maintained that scrutiny of Chinese-linked education programs should not be interpreted as opposition to Chinese teachers or Mandarin instruction, but as an examination of possible political influence behind the programs.

​The Department of National Defense (DND) has also defended scrutiny of foreign state-backed academic and cultural exchange programs, saying transparency is necessary to protect academic integrity and national security.

​Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. has raised concerns about Jinan University’s links to Chinese-language teacher training and its academic work questioning Philippine sovereignty over Batanes.

​The DND has denied targeting Chinese schools, saying its concerns involve possible foreign influence rather than Chinese-language education itself.

title: ‘Bird’s-eye view’ enhances disaster response and climate resilience
summary: WHEN a major tropical cyclone tears across the archipelago, roads submerge, bridges collapse, and terrestrial communications often fail. In those critical early hours, emergency responders face a dangerous information void. The quickest way
content:
WHEN a major tropical cyclone tears across the archipelago, roads submerge, bridges collapse, and terrestrial communications often fail. In those critical early hours, emergency responders face a dangerous information void. The quickest way to see that deluge is not by road or air, but from low Earth orbit.

The Philippine Space Agency (PhilSA), satellite data underpins both immediate post-impact emergency operations and multidecade resilience planning. Tasked with managing the country’s Earth observation satellites, PhilSA has evolved from its origins in DOSTled research initiatives, moving beyond experimental scientific pursuits to become an indispensable pillar of the nation’s disaster risk reduction and climate adaptation infrastructure.

While the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) relies on meteorological orbiters to track typhoons, rain bands, and atmospheric dynamics in real time, PhilSA leverages Earth observation imagery to assess ground impact. The agency generates disaster extent maps that delineate the footprint of floods, landslides, volcanic activity, and earthquake damage.

*   [Mayabang talaga!](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/business/top-business/mayabang-talaga/2442100)

A satellite pass offers a panoramic, high-altitude view that ground networks cannot replicate. A single sweep captures entire river basins, provinces, and inaccessible hazard zones, allowing national and local disaster agencies to dispatch relief, position search-and-rescue teams, and allocate capital where damage is concentrated.

“Satellites provide a bird’s-eye view of disasters that groundbased systems cannot, allowing them to monitor large areas in a single pass. This complements ground observations by providing a broader picture of what is happening across provinces, regions, or even the entire country, especially when access on the ground is limited or unsafe,” Gay Jane Perez, Director General of PhilSA told The Manila Times.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

The Science and Technology page asked about the contributions of PhilSA to disaster monitoring and management and how the agency transforms raw downlinked satellite passes into actionable geospatial information.

_**TMT: How quickly can satellite data be turned into useful information during a disaster?**_

Dr. Perez: Satellite data can be turned into useful information within hours, depending on the satellite, weather conditions, and the availability of imagery. Once new images are received, PhilSA processes and analyzes them to produce disaster extent maps and other geospatial products that can be shared with government agencies and local government units for response operations.

*   ![Image 1: Is a compromise agreement sufficient to determine child custody?](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/08/1252137.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Is a compromise agreement sufficient to determine child custody?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/legal-advice/is-a-compromise-agreement-sufficient-to-determine-child-custody/2442021)

Depending on the satellite data to be processed, the turnaround time for processing and distributing datasets can go as fast as 6-8 hours after data acquisition. Longer processing times usually stem from huge volumes of incoming data, but the main limitation is the availability of usable satellite data.

**TMT: What are the biggest limitations of using satellites for disaster monitoring?**

Dr. Perez: Satellite data is a powerful tool for disaster monitoring, but it also has limitations.

Optical satellites cannot capture clear images through thick cloud cover, which is common during tropical storms and typhoons.

*   ![Image 2: 10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252382.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[10 special non-working days declared for Oct](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/regions/10-special-non-working-days-declared-for-oct/2442158)

In these situations, Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellites are especially useful because they can collect images through clouds and at night.

However, SAR also has limitations. Flood detection can be less accurate in dense urban areas and heavily vegetated locations because buildings and vegetation can affect how radar signals are reflected. This is why satellitederived maps are often validated with ground observations and other sources of information.

Another limitation is the revisit time. Satellites do not continuously observe the same location, so the availability of imagery depends on when a satellite passes over an affected area and whether usable data is acquired.

**TMT: How important are Philippine-owned satellites to disaster preparedness?**

*   ![Image 3: Man arrested after breaching NAIA security to reunite with OFW wife](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/09/1252636.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Man arrested after breaching NAIA security to reunite with OFW wife](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/09/news/man-arrested-after-breaching-naia-security-to-reunite-with-ofw-wife/2442354)

Dr. Perez: Having sovereign satellites allows us to control when, where, and how often it can gather data, without having to rely on other countries. Besides some exceptions, the Philippines has to pay for high resolution images, the cost of which can go up to millions of pesos. We would also have to wait in ‘line’ as with other countries’ requests, and accept the available coverage.

With sovereign satellites, the country can prioritize imaging its own territory first, focusing on areas of high relevance rather than competing with global demands.

Although the Philippines is part of several groups—such as theInternational Charter Space and Major Disasters (Disasters Charter) andSentinel Asia—which provide free acquisition and transmission of satellite data in the event of a disaster, that data is still reliant on whether there are foreign satellites that have passed over the country at the time of disaster.

Sovereign satellites provide faster access to data, lower longterm costs, and the ability to immediately task satellites according to the situation. Having sovereign satellites will also build local expertise and infrastructure, as these satellites will need Filipinos who can operate, analyze, and use the data.

**TMT: What can Philippine satellites do today that they could not do a few years ago?**

Dr. Perez: The Philippines has significantly strengthened its homegrown Earth observation capabilities over the past few years, providing locally managed data for environmental monitoring, agriculture, maritime domain awareness, and disaster response.

PhilSA also has greater capacity to process and analyze satellite imagery into geospatial products, such as disaster extent maps, that can be shared with government agencies and local government units more quickly. Looking ahead, the MULA satellite will further enhance this capability by providing higher-resolution multispectral images,, supporting more detailed monitoring of land, water, forests, and coastal areas.

**TMT: How is artificial intelligence being used to analyze satellite images?**

Dr. Perez: Trained artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms can be used to detect changes in satellite images. By combining several satellite images of the same location, taken at different dates, trained AI models can spot changes and help confirm events such as flooding.

These models can also process massive amounts of satellite data semi-automatically and simultaneously, speeding up mapping and enabling responders to act faster.

**TMT: What is the biggest gap in the Philippines’ use of space technology for disaster preparedness?**

Dr. Perez: One of the Philippines’ key challenges is ensuring that satellite data is translated into timely, actionable information for decision-makers at the national and local levels. While satellite imagery is increasingly available, maximizing its value requires strong ground validation, data sharing across agencies, technical capacity, and the integration of satellite information into disaster risk reduction and response systems. A MULA constellation, composed of multiple follow-on satellites, would allow more frequent revisits and allow us to get more timely data during disasters.

Continued investments in local space infrastructure, Earth observation capabilities, and geospatial expertise will help strengthen the country’s disaster preparedness and resilience.

# Help 88-year old Veteran Keep His Home After Marriage Fraud

UPDATE 9/8: Our retainer is gone and we are in need of funds to replenish the trust account with the attorney. We are in the middle of the discovery process, and while the wife continues to hide assets, we are forced to subpoena her bank and investment accounts which costs more money. The lawyer will ask the court that she pay our attorney fees, it likely won’t be granted until the trial in February. By then we may be out a lawyer because we can’t pay him. UPDATE 6/25: We have retained an attorney! We are continuing to seek donations for when the retainer runs out. Due to family donations, we need to raise less money than originally anticipated, so we’ve lowered our fundraiser from $15,000 to $10,000. My 88-year-old father is a victim of elder abuse and marriage fraud that may leave him homeless and destitute. I am setting up this GoFundMe to pay for his legal representation, likely the only way he will be able to keep his home of 23 years. Please hear our story: About six years ago, my father was pursued through an online dating site by a woman named Candy. In a matter of days and through very limited communication, she convinced my father she was in love with him, asked for his address, hopped on a Greyhound, and moved into his small home. Within two weeks they were married at the courthouse. Candy is a citizen of the People’s Republic of China, had been in and out of the country on a B2 tourist visa, and is 22 years younger than my father. Immediately after the marriage, Candy began the US citizenship process with my father's sponsorship. Upon her demand, my father took out a series of small loans to hire her an immigration attorney even though she started working. She began to receive social security spousal support, and was also receiving money from her Chinese pension. In spite of her income, my father continued to pay all their bills himself, including the mortgage and utilities. When Candy took a trip to Hawaii (with her friends and her own income), my father disclosed to me that he did not feel safe with her. I learned she had become increasingly hostile towards him, calling him fat, denying him food, referring to him as “the sickly old man” behind his back, and at times being aggressive enough that he would choose to sleep and/or sit in his car until she left the house. Her favorite insult was "garbage husband." It became increasingly clear that Candy was exploiting my father. At one point she approached him with a Quit Claim deed to transmute his sole property into community property. In the throes of an abusive relationship, my father felt like he had no choice but to sign the deed. Now my father's home of 23 years - and its equity - belongs to her as well. About a year ago, Candy started stealing money from my father, and he found himself overwhelmed with not being able to pay the bills that supported them both. By this time, my father had long been beaten down from the abuse, but in a last ditch effort he built up the nerve to ask Candy to return the stolen money and sign a quit claim to give back his house - she said only if he gave her $80,000! My brother and I were relieved when my father made the decision to file for divorce, and we become increasingly involved on his behalf. We prepared court paperwork for him as he cannot identify the correct documents. My father can't type and his handwriting is slow, so filling out forms is also challenging. He is a poor communicator. He often nods off at court. Recognizing that my father cannot represent himself in court, a judge ordered a settlement conference, which went nowhere fast because Candy still demands $80,000. My father does not have any money laying around, and is leveraged to the hilt with debt from the marriage (all in his name), so he couldn't borrow money to pay her even if he wanted. As a National Guard veteran, senior, and low-income individual, my father is eligible for free legal advice three times over, but what he needs is representation. Because of his advanced age and the complexity of his case, he does not have the mental capacity to represent himself. He has long been unable to organize and process decent amounts of detailed information without assistance. He is overwhelmed at the thought of losing his house, which flusters him even more. If he loses his house, not only does he face homelessness, but more importantly he loses the property's equity that was intended to cover his long-term nursing care, care that he is starting to need, and the emotional toll of being forced to sell and move out of his house would surely be the end for him. We appreciate every donation, big and small. The money raised will go directly to his legal representation. Please feel free to contact me with questions or more details.

Abhaya started as disaster recovery - how do communities rebuild communication when the towers are down and the power's out? But we realized something profound: the same tools that help neighborhoods coordinate after a hurricane are exactly what we need when authoritarians try to silence us. Like the protective Abhaya Mudra, this system creates a shield against the "evil eye" of surveillance while becoming a helpful digital companion that guides and empowers our communities. Drawing inspiration from Buckminster Fuller's vision of global cooperation for humanity's benefit, Abhaya is designed as the foundation for communities to work together toward a more equitable future. The ecosystem operates through five interconnected elements: The Five Core Components: • Tor + Mobile based Mesh Networks: Messages that flow around censorship like water • Mesh Based Distributed Storage: Truth that lives everywhere so it can't be destroyed • Mesh Based Distributed Computation Service: AI-capable shared processing power for communities to solve their own challenges • Sensor/Peripheral IO: User Controlled Eyes and ears embedded in the network • Mesh Federation: Connecting local networks into unstoppable global resistance History demonstrates the need "The ultimate measure of a man is not where he stands in moments of comfort and convenience, but where he stands at times of challenge and controversy." - MLK Jr. After Hurricane Katrina, communities learned they couldn't wait for official help. Hong Kong protesters used mesh networks when the government tried to cut them off. Iranian women shared videos of police brutality when the state blocked social media. Puerto Ricans coordinated mutual aid through amateur radio when Maria destroyed the grid. The pattern is clear: when systems fail - whether from natural disasters or deliberate suppression - communities need tools to build their own infrastructure. Communities united in purpose and vision can be powerful. Your Support = Digital Fearlessness When you contribute to Abhaya, you're investing in infrastructure that makes communities fearless. No CEO can sell it. No government can buy it. No algorithm can suppress it. No storm can wash it away. Every dollar helps us turn individual devices into collective power. Like Powell said - we're not waiting for someone to save us. We're using what's already in our hands to build the infrastructure of fearlessness. Fund the network that makes communities fearless. Join the Build: Technologists Wanted We're assembling an international team of developers and engineers who understand that code is power, and power should belong to the people. If you're a technologist looking to put your skills toward meaningful resistance, this is how you push back against authoritarianism and corporate overreach. We need volunteers with expertise in: • Android & iOS Development • Onion Router, I2P, Freenet protocols • DevOps/SecOps fluent in Dark Web technologies • Distributed Systems Design • AI Systems Engineering This is open-source work with no revenue model - Abhaya is designed to be free for all communities. For technologists feeling the weight of current events, it's a concrete way to turn skills into direct action and fulfill civic duty through code. Ready to put your shoulder to the wheel of progress? content:
We are 100 families taking on the CCP - and we need your help.

我們是「皇家鑄幣廠居民協會」，由約一百戶職工家庭組成。我們懇請你伸出援手。

In 2018, our homes-key-worker flats in Tower Hamlets were sold in a secretive deal to the People's Republic of China. We had no say. No warning. And now, we face living under the shadow of a hostile superpower.

2018年，我們居住的Tower Hamlets地段，在未經通知、無任何諮詢下，被秘密售予中國政府。我們無從置喙，如今更面對一個敵對政權的威脅。

The UK Government is expected to approve plans to build the largest embassy in Europe - right here, at Royal Mint Court, next to the Tower of London… and directly on top of our homes.

英國政府即將批准於倫敦塔旁的皇家鑄幣廠（Royal Mint Court）興建歐洲最大規模的中國大使館，預定地點正正位於我們所居之上。

This is not just a planning dispute.

我們擔憂的不僅是一項城市規劃決策，而是一場關乎國家安全、人身安全與基本權利的危機。

China has never shown any regard for our safety - and now the Government and the Metropolitan Police have abandoned us too.

自2018年起，中國政府從未就此提供明確回應，我們甚至不知道會否被驅逐、是否仍能繼續安居於此。而如今，政府與執法機關也對我們置之不理。

We are the Royal Mint Court Residents Association. People backed our previous Crowdfunder campaign that helped pay for a barrister to present our evidence including an independent security assessment showing the serious risks to us from a terror attack on the mega-embassy.

我們是「皇家鑄幣廠居民協會」。我們之前的眾籌活動獲得許多人的支持，資助我們聘請資深大律師提交證據，包括一份獨立的安全評估報告，指出超級大使館可能帶來的恐襲風險。

We are now launching an urgent legal challenge - a Judicial Review - to change the law and stop this injustice.

我們現在正展開一項緊急法律挑戰 — 即司法覆核 — 希望改變現行法律，阻止這場不公。

We need your help to protect our community from the mighty Chinese Communist Party.

我們需要你的幫助，去保護我們的社區，免受強大的中國共產黨威脅。

Whatever you can spare us, will help David stand-up to Goliath.

無論你能捐出多少，都能幫助大衛對抗歌利亞。

We are seeking to pursue a Judicial Review because we have believed all along that the planning process has been flawed. Here are some of the reasons we think are likely to be relevant:

我們決定提起司法覆核，是因為我們始終認為整個規劃程序存在問題。以下是我們認為可能相關的一些原因：

“Closed mind”: Ministers may have signalled early approval to China, before formal procedures were followed, breaking the law and abusing planning powers. In a similar vein, objections disappeared after UK ministers returned from Beijing. Residents have felt like pawns in a geopolitical game since the start.

預設立場：部長們可能在正式程序開始前就向中方表示支持，違反法律並濫用規劃權力。在部長們從北京回來之後，原有的反對聲音突然消失。居民們從一開始就覺得自己成了地緣政治博弈中的棋子。

Security concerns: Building a fortified embassy with homes on site and critical infrastructure nearby, ignoring espionage concerns and the real human risk to dissidents, is indefensible.

安全隱患：在住宅區內及重要基礎設施附近建設高度防禦的大使館，無視間諜活動與對異見人士的人身威脅，完全不能接受。

Procedural unfairness: We were shut out of the process. No consultation. No transparency. No respect for the people who live here.

程序不公：我們被完全排除在決策過程之外。無諮詢、無透明、無對居民的尊重。

Legitimate expectation: We were promised due process and protection. We got silence.

合理期望落空：我們被承諾將獲程序保障與保護，實際卻是得不到任何保障。

What’s wrong with the embassy plan?

We still live here. 100 families. Nurses, teachers, pensioners. Our 100 homes are on land now owned by the Chinese government. That means the Chinese ambassador is our landlord - with rights to enter our homes.

我們仍然住在這裡 ，足足一百戶家庭，包括護士、教師、退休人士。我們的一百個住所現已位於中國政府擁有的土地上。這代表中國大使成為我們的業主，有權進入我們的住所。

China refuses to answer us. Since 2018, we’ve begged for assurances: will we be evicted? Will we be safe? Can we stay? Beijing’s answer: not until we get planning permission. This refusal, and the proposal to install a temporary style wooden boundary fence as a dividing line, raises fears that the Chinese Government intends to take back the entire 100 apartments at St Mary Graces Court once they secure diplomatic status for the site, leaving us homeless.

中國拒絕回應我們的訴求。自2018年起，我們不斷尋求保證：我們會被驅逐嗎？我們是否安全？我們能否繼續居住？北京的答覆是：等規劃許可下來再說。這種拒絕，以及擬議中以臨時木欄分隔的做法，讓我們擔心中國政府一旦取得外交地位，將會收回整個St Mary Graces Court的100個單位，使我們流離失所。

This embassy is a fortress. It’s not a normal diplomatic building. It will have secret communications centres, fortified walls, and surveillance technology that can monitor our entire estate, even our bedrooms. It will also stand on top of critical UK cables that MI5 warn are a security risk to the UK.

這座大使館是一個堡壘，並非普通的外交建築。它將設有秘密通訊設施、加固圍牆、監控技術，可監視整個屋苑，甚至包括我們的睡房。而它的地基下方，更有英國重要電纜 ，MI5曾警告這是對國家安全的威脅。

The UK Government knows the risk - and ignored it. Our independent security report warns that this site puts families and national security at risk. Even the UK’s Head of Counter-Terrorism originally objected - citing threats to residents and dissidents. But since ministers returned from Beijing, objections have mysteriously vanished.

英國政府明知有風險，卻選擇無視。我們的獨立安全報告指出，該地點將危害居民與國家安全。甚至連英國反恐部門首長最初也曾反對 ， 指出對居民與異見人士的威脅。但自從部長從北京回來後，這些反對聲音神秘地消失。

Ministers made no mention of the 100 families living here. We are alarmed that the letters from Home Secretary Yvette Cooper and Foreign Secretary David Lammy have ignored the fact that UK families live in 100 apartments on the land that is actually part of Royal Mint court - and is owned by the Chinese government. Our Resident’s Chairman has personally appealed to ministers, submitted the full Crilly Consultants security report, and our plight has appeared in The Times, FT, BBC, CNN, and more. What is happening to democratic accountability in this country?

部長們從未提及這裡有一百戶居民。我們對內政大臣Yvette Cooper及外交大臣David Lammy的信件感到震驚，因為他們完全忽略了皇家鑄幣廠的土地上住有英國公民、100個家庭。我們的居民協會主席曾親自致函部長、提交完整的Crilly安全報告，而我們的處境亦已被《泰晤士報》、《金融時報》、BBC、CNN等多間媒體報導。英國民主問責制度何在？

The first duty of the UK government is to protect its citizens. We understand the UK’s diplomatic obligations - but not at the expense of its own people. The refusal to acknowledge the basic risks of housing a high-security foreign embassy on top of a residential block is deeply troubling. It appears the government is prioritising relations with Beijing over the safety of its own citizens.

英國政府的首要職責是保護其國民。我們明白外交義務，但不能以犧牲本國人民為代價。將一個高安全級別的外國大使館設於住宅區上方，而拒絕承認基本風險，是極度令人不安的。

It’s not just about us. Dissidents, including Hong Kongers, Uyghurs, Tibetans, Taiwanese and Chinese exile communities are terrified. They’ve told us they no longer feel safe protesting outside the site, and on British soil. Their presence, and ours, will be met with constant surveillance and intimidation by a regime known to harass and threaten activists - even abroad.

這件事不僅關係到我們。流亡港人、維吾爾人、西藏人、台灣人及中國異見社群皆感到恐懼。他們表示不再敢在該地點或英國土地上公開抗議。他們與我們一樣，將面對來自這個以恐嚇異見者聞名的政權的持續監控與威嚇。

The people have spoken, and they support us.

人民已經發聲，並支持我們。

On 8 February 2025, thousands of British citizens - including Hong Kongers, Uyghurs, Tibetans, Taiwanese and Chinese pro-democracy activists, and human rights campaigners - gathered outside Royal Mint Court in protest against this embassy.

2025年2月8日，數以千計的英國公民 ，包括港人、維吾爾人、西藏人、台灣人、中國民主人士與人權倡議者， 齊集皇家鑄幣廠，抗議中國大使館計劃。

They were joined by cross-party MPs, journalists, and allies. Together, they said NO to the Chinese embassy, and YES to democratic values, safety, and justice.

他們與跨黨派議員、記者及盟友並肩站立，一同說出明確立場：反對中國大使館，支持民主、安全與公義。

Further mass protests followed on 15 March, 3 May, and 14 June - showing growing national resistance to the plan.

3月15日、5月3日及6月14日亦舉行後續大型集會，反對聲浪日益壯大。

They continue to protest, and have made it clear: they won’t stop until this mega-embassy deal is over.

抗議仍在持續，並清楚表示：他們不會停止，直至該項目取消為止。

But the Government is not listening.

但政府並未聆聽我們的訴求。

So now, we go to court.

所以現在，我們只有訴諸法庭。

But we need your help - fast.

但我們需要您的協助 - 迅速的協助。

The legal fees for a Judicial Review are beyond the reach of ordinary families. But with your help, we can stand up to both Beijing and Whitehall.

司法覆核的法律費用遠超普通家庭的負擔。但在您的幫助下，我們能夠與北京和英國政府對抗。

This case is about more than one building. It’s about:

這宗案件關乎的遠不止一座建築。它關乎：

Protecting British citizens from state overreach

保護英國公民免受國家權力的侵害

Defending UK democracy from foreign influence

捍衛英國的民主，抵抗外國影響

Challenging backroom deals that put power over people

挑戰那些將權力凌駕於人民之上的秘密交易

If we succeed, we won’t just protect our homes. We’ll set a precedent that no foreign government can build on British soil without respecting British citizens and British values.

如若成功，我們不僅能保護我們的家園，我們更是創下先例：任何外國政府不得在罔顧英國公民和英國價值的前提下在英國土地上建造任何建築。

Will you stand with us?

您願意與我們並肩作戰嗎？

Please chip in whatever you can. £10. £100. £1,000. Every penny goes to legal costs to take this to court. We are a group of teachers, nurses, shop workers and pensioners. We don’t have the Chinese Communist Party’s millions - but with your help, we do have people power.

請您捐出任何您能負擔的金額 — 不論是 £10，£100 還是 £1,000。每一分錢都將用於支付法律費用，讓我們將此案帶上法庭。我們只是一群教師、護士、店員和退休人士。雖然我們沒有中國共產黨的龐大資金 — 但在您的幫助下，我們擁有的是人民的力量。

Share this far and wide.

請廣傳此訊息。

Donate if you can.

如有行力，請捐款。

Stand up for democracy.

為民主發聲。

Because if they can do this to us, they can do it to anyone.

唇亡齒寒。

PLEASE NOTE

請注意：

This is a secure UK-based platform, fully registered and subject to UK law.

這是一個安全的英國平台，註冊並受英國法律管轄。

It is widely used to support political and legal campaigns, including by MPs, NGOs, and grassroots movements - some of which are openly critical of the Chinese government.

該平台廣泛用於支持政治和法律活動，包括國會議員、非政府組織和基層運動 — 包括曾公開批評中國政府的政治活動。

The platform offers full transparency, with public donation records and payment processing via Stripe or PayPal.

該平台提供完全透明的捐款記錄，並通過 Stripe 或 PayPal 處理支付。

There is no history of censorship or compliance with pressure from the Chinese state.

台以往並無自我審查紀錄，也未曾屈從於中國的壓力。

It adheres strictly to GDPR regulations, ensuring donor and campaigner data is protected.

平台嚴格遵守 GDPR 規範，確保捐款者和活動者的數據安全。

About your donations

關於您的捐款

2.95% + 0.25 of each donation goes to the platform; 100% of the remaining funds will be used to cover legal costs.

每筆捐款將扣除 2.95% 加 £0.25 之平台手續費，其餘款項將全數用以支付法律相關費用。

If the legal case is dismissed, your donation will be directed to charity unless you request a refund. If you would like your donation returned, please email us. We will calculate and refund your contribution (with platform fee deducted).

如法律訴訟最終被駁回，捐款將撥捐予慈善機構，除非閣下主動申請退款。如欲索回捐款，請電郵至，我們將在扣除平台手續費後，計算並退還閣下之捐款。

About campaign updates

關於活動更新

We will post updates every two weeks, which you can follow directly on this page.

我們每兩週更新一次進展，您可以直接於此頁面查看。

content:
***When donation, make as anonymous if you wish to hide the donator's name and make the TIPS to 0.00***

While US-China tensions continue to escalate and the November presidential elections loom near, as Hongkongers living in the United States (or any informed person in the world), we must not forget or turn a blind eye to the CCP’s continuous oppression on Hongkongers and other minority groups in China, such as Uyghurs, Tibetans, and Mongolians. With the promulgation of the new National Security Law on June 30, 2020, the government has since been arresting and charging dissidents with these vaguely-worded laws that may entail life imprisonment. In the past month alone, 12 Hong Kongers fleeing protest-related charges have been detained in China and denied meetings with lawyers since August 23, 2020; Legislative Council elections had been postponed a year in the name of “public health concerns” amidst a mass arrest of candidates; media mogul Jimmy Lai, who runs the only pro-democratic print newspaper in Hong Kong, has been arrested with the National Security Law; and the Education Bureau has begun actively censoring content they deemed politically incorrect in Liberal Studies textbooks, including concepts like “civil disobedience” and “separation of powers”, and images of Lennon Walls. Up until today, the administration has arrested more than 10,000 Hong Kongers, charged over 2,200, deployed water cannons, fired more than 16,000 tear gas canisters and over 10,000 rubber bullets against its own people. Freedom of speech, freedom of assembly and political rights as we knew it have been thoroughly eroded.

11月的美國總統大選逐漸逼近，中美關係日漸緊張，作為居住在美國的香港人或是在這個世界上任何有良知的人，面對中共對香港、維吾爾族、藏族和蒙古族的持續壓逼，我們不能容忍，更不能視而不見。自2020年6月30日頒布《國家安全法》以來，政府持續逮捕異見人​​士，並以措辭含糊的法律起訴抗爭者，香港的司法制度已經徹底淪為政府的打壓工具。及後更有12名香港抗爭者為了逃離這種不公義的審判欲流亡台灣，卻被中共非法拘捕。他們無法與律師會面，音訊全無。而香港人僅有的發聲方法——立法會選舉，卻因為「公共衛生風險」而被推遲一年；同時間，大批候選人被逮捕或是被拒絕參選。作為香港唯一異見紙媒《蘋果日報》的老闆黎智英被警方高調逮捕，《蘋果日報》總部更被大肆搜查。教育局亦積極審查通識科教科書中所謂的「政治不正確」內容，例如「公民抗命」和「三權分立」的概念，以及連儂牆相片。到今天為止，已經有超過10,000多名香港人被捕、2,200多人被起訴，警方向市民發射了超過16,000枚催淚彈和10,000多發橡皮子彈，令香港人長期生活在恐懼中。香港人的言論自由、集會自由和政治權利已被徹底侵蝕。

In light of the deteriorating situation, we plan to kickstart a new round of postcard campaign urging Congress to pass two bills related to Hong Kong as soon as possible - Hong Kong Safe Harbor Act (H.R.7415/S.4110), and Hong Kong People’s Freedom and Choice Act (H.R.7428/S.4229):

鑑於情況日益惡化，我們希望透過郵寄明信片給國會議員的方式，呼籲他們盡快通過兩項與香港有關的法案 —— 香港安全港法案 (H.R.7415 / S.4110) 和香港人民自由與選擇法(H.R.7428 / S.4229):

The Hong Kong Safe Harbor Act will designate certain Hong Kong residents who are victims of persecution or who have a well-founded fear of future persecution because of their peaceful political activities as Priority 2 refugees (excluded from refugee cap), allowing them and their spouses, children, parents to apply to the U.S. Refugee Admissions Program for protection. (Click here for more details)

《香港安全港法案》將指定某些遭受迫害，或因其參與和平的政治活動而感到恐懼的香港居民列為「優先級別2」的難民，且不受每年限額限制，亦允許他們及其配偶、子女、父母向「美國難民接納計劃」申請庇護。(詳情請瀏覽)

The Hong Kong People's Freedom and Choice Act will provide Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Hong Kongers, maintain Hong Kong’s status as autonomous for the purposes of immigration, provide special and expedited status for certain high-skilled Hong Kongers as well as expedite Permanent Resident status for Hong Kongers residing in the US. (Click here for more details)

《香港人民自由與選擇法》會為香港人提供臨時保護身份（TPS），維持香港在移民方面的自治地位，亦為部分香港專業人仕提供特殊和快速的身份，並加快辦理香港人的美國永久居民(綠卡)身份的程序。(詳情請瀏覽)

In our last postcard campaign pushing for the Hong Kong Human Rights and Democracy Act, we delivered over 3000 postcards to Congress. We aren’t part of any formal organization and do not have operation funds. We desperately call for your contribution again to help us deliver these postcards to Congress, to remind them of Hong Kong’s urgent situation and urge them to take immediate action. Your contribution would support our printing and delivery costs. Thank you so much!

在上一次推動《香港人權與民主法》的明信片運動中，我們向國會送出了超過3000張的明信片。我們不是任何正式組織的成員，也沒有運營資金，所以我們竭誠呼籲您為我們提供資金，並幫助我們將這些明信片送交您們所屬的國會議員，提醒他們香港的緊急狀況，並呼籲他們立即採取行動。所有受到的捐款將支持我們的打印和交付成本。萬分感謝！

# Help A #MeToo Survivor and Daughter Win Their Case

(中文版見後）What I’ve experienced isn’t what any woman should ever go through. First there was the violence of non-consensual sex forced on me, followed by lies and denial. Then, rare moments of hope, followed by setbacks tinged with revenge from a father whose fear of revealing truth drives him to deny his child’s existence. This child is my daughter. For 20 years I’ve hidden the nightmare involving her origin by my silence, partly due to the sense of shame and partly because the father of my child is a influential public figure. Till the rapist has pushed us to a corner by threatening our existence with vicious conspiracy theories.（我經歷了任何一位女性都不該經歷的事情。先是遭遇性侵，接著還要面對謊言、抵賴和詆毀。過去20年來，間或閃現的希望，卻因我女兒的生父拒絕承認這孩子的存在，而淹沒在長久的幻滅中。過去20年來，我一直對女兒的身世三緘其口，讓一段揮之不去的夢魘深藏內心，一方面出於羞辱感，另一方面無法面對孩子的生父作為一個公眾人物給我心靈帶來的扭曲。）With your help, the truth of our experience will be told. When it is, I hope justice will prevail. This is why I’m emerging from the shadows.（因您伸出援手，我將得以說出這段真實的經歷。當真相大白的那一天到來，我希望正義能夠隨之彰顯。）(Charlotte and me in 2003)In 2000, I was a journalist working for a local Chinese newspaper in Los Angeles. I was assigned to interview a famous Chinese dissident, a political refugee in America, who people called the “Godfather of the Democratic Movement in China.” I wrote the story, but in doing so, my life was changed forever by his sexual assault of me.（2000年，身為洛杉磯當地一家中文媒體記者的我，被派去採訪一位著名的中國異議人士，也是我本人非常敬仰的政治流亡者、一位被視為「中國民主運動之父」的風雲人物。我完成了採訪任務，然而我的個人生活卻因今生與他這唯一的遭逢而徹底脫軌。）Let’s just say, nine months after I did that story, I gave birth to my daughter, who bore no resemblance to my then-husband. My husband knew why since I’d told him about the sexual assault after it happened. My marriage ended, and my life as a single mom began. To protect my daughter and me from possible backlash about how she was conceived and her father’s identity, I kept my ordeal quiet. The two of us moved to Hong Kong.（在我做了那次採訪的9個月之後，我的女兒降生了。她跟我當時的丈夫長得一點也不像，而我丈夫也並不感到驚訝，因為我早跟他坦白了我遭遇性侵的事。我的婚姻其實從那時起已名存實亡，我作為一個單親母親的生涯也即將開始。為了遠離各種因孩子身世而產生的猜忌，讓我和孩子可以過安靜而屬於自己的生活，同時也為了可以就近得到父母家人的幫忙照顧，我帶著孩子離開了美國，赴香港尋找發展機會。） Through the years I never thought about contacting my daughter's biological father, whom I met only once. I didn’t consider doing this even after I lost my job as an editor in 2012. But then a former colleague, Beifeng, left Hong Kong for the United States. He’d criticized me for "depriving the child the right to be recognized by her father," and later persuaded me to let him bring a lock of my daughter’s hair, wrapped it in tissue paper, that he took with him to the United States. （多年來，我從未想過要聯絡孩子的生父，那個我只見過一面的人，哪怕是2012年我失業的時候也沒萌生這個打算。我根本已經忘記了這個人，要不是當時正要動身赴美的前同事北風（我告訴了他我的孩子生父是誰，但沒有讓他知道詳情，他也沒有探問）批評我「剝奪孩子認父的權利」。他太太當即揪了孩子幾根頭髮，用手紙包了起來。） (drawing by Charlotte)Months later, my heart sank when Beifeng reported back to me that this man had denied everything, even the possibility of knowing me, let alone the possibility of having fathered a child. He’d committed this horrible crime against me, but he refused to acknowledge this truth. For to accept that he’d fathered a daughter, he’d have to admit how she came to existence. It appeared that he was refusing to allow his carefully crafted story about his “heroic” life to be marred by acknowledging his daughter’s existence.（幾個月之後，北風帶來消息並深表意外地說，孩子的生父得知自己可能有個孩子時的反應，竟是敷衍和閃躲，好像根本不可能有這回事一樣。他當然寧肯忘記自己做過的事，但真相怎麼能因你不想面對就可以不承認、孩子怎麼可以就這樣當她不存在呢？就像他後來在郵件裡提到的，他所關切的，是這事將來在他的回憶錄裡該怎麼寫，而不是他身為人父應該盡什麼責。他在意的只是他自己英雄般的人生，無論如何不能留下任何污點。）After this news reached me, I was diagnosed with clinical depression and started to see a doctor regularly. Professionally, however, I had to appear calm and collected so I could earn a living that would support the two of us. I worked as a freelance writer and translator, while also raising my daughter on my own.（我聞訊心裡沉了一下，不久開始意識恍惚，甚至試過下班下車記不起回家的方向。我遠在北京的母親聽說之後，在電話的另一頭啜泣得聲音哽咽。2013年2月，我被確診患上抑鬱症。失業更兼病倒，令我們母女的生計雪上加霜，這期間我成為自由撰稿人，還要硬撐著努力譯書維持生計。好在偶爾有父母幫手、妹妹接濟一下，才度過了一段危機。） (drawing by Charlotte)Five years later, in 2018, in the midst of #MeToo movement, when sexual abuse and harassment were receiving public attention globally, rumors spread online about this famous Chinese man having fathered an illegitimate child. At that point, I contacted him by phone from Hong Kong and boldly asked for child support.（一晃又過了5年，時間到了2018年，在#MeToo（「我也是受害者」）運動的聲浪中，性侵和性騷擾現象的普遍存在引起了全球性輿論關注。在此期間，網上首次出現了對我女兒的生父「不認親」的議論。已變得反應遲緩的我這才開始應對，邁出了主動聯繫孩子生父這一步。）He agreed to a DNA test that was performed privately in Washington D.C.., The DNA results proved that he was Charlotte's father. The person who shared the results with him said that he had responded positively to having a daughter. Accordingly, when I contacted him again, he promised to assist us by at least paying for her education. But later on, since I would not change my tone on the unhappy encounter with him in the past, he decided to deny being Charlotte’s father and began to challenge the DNA results, shirked his responsibility as her biological father, and ignored that I was a victim of his violent sexual assault.（他於是主動提出做個DNA鑑定，並指定了一位背景相當可靠的前白宮幕僚做中間人，在華盛頓特區進行了DNA樣本的收集與鑑定。結果出來後，中間人率先通知我，說結果證明魏先生是孩子的生父無疑，並告訴我，魏先生對鑑定結果表示認可並顯得「很開心」。據此，在我與孩子的生父再次聯繫時，他表示自己起碼會負擔孩子的大學學費。但真到了時候他又變卦了，甚至仗著沒有把DNA鑑定結果如約給我們，便想將已經做過DNA鑑定這事也想賴掉。） (drawing by Charlotte)The rest of the story is detailed in Huaizhao Liu v. Jingsheng Wei, case #1:19-cv-03344, which was heard in the Washington, D.C. federal court. Charlotte’s father managed to find the funds necessary to hire a high-powered defense attorney to help him to deny both our dignity and his basic obligations of paternity.（後來的事情見華盛頓特區聯邦法院卷宗（Case Number 1:19-cv-03344）。我女兒的生父大手筆聘請了專攻白領犯罪辯護的名牌大狀為自己的辯護律師，竭力搬弄法律條文進行技術性規避，想就此永遠掩蓋真相，踐踏我們母女的權益與尊嚴。）We believe that Charlotte’s biological father should be forced to keep his promise of supporting her education, and we are asking that he release the DNA test results to us. His 19-year old daughter deserves to know the truth.（我們堅信，法庭應該為這位竭力否認已經做過親子鑑定的生父驗明正身，然後強制他履行他的諾言，承擔他女兒的學費。我們堅信，他19歲的女兒有權利知曉真相。）The weight of evidence is on our side, but we risk losing the lawsuit that we are filing against him if we cannot raise the money we need to hire an attorney who is as capable as his lawyer. What is at risk is Charlotte's right to a quality education, along with the legally binding acknowledgement of his paternity.（儘管我們掌握活生生的證據，但如果籌不到聘請律師的費用，單憑我們自訴，將無法應對複雜的陪審團庭審程序。立案至今一年多來，被告採取躲和拖的戰術，先是躲傳票，然後提出「司法管轄權」爭議逼我們撤案，一計不成又援引「多國籍」條款，將案子從特區高等法院轉移到聯邦法院。） (Charlotte drawing)With your assistance – with your contributions – we intend to hire an attorney who is experienced in sexual assault and paternity cases. We hope to win this #MeToo case and pursue respectful, equal and democratic human relationship in Chinese community. （您的捐助將幫助我們聘請到專攻性侵案和親子案官司的律師，幫我們贏得這場事關尊嚴、平等、人權以及人性的人身傷害官司，並藉此推動美國的華人社區乃至全球華人的觀念進步與行為的現代化。）Here are some online stories and commentary about this, in Chinese: （以下是部分有關此案的中文文章：）https://www.storm.mg/article/2891777?mode=whole廖亦武：《魏京生DNA認親案》(by Liao Yiwu, award winner of Human Rights Watch Hellman-Hammett Grant 2003, the German Geschwister-Scholl-Preis 2011 and the Peace Prize of the German Book Trade 2012.)（作者/廖亦武，詩人、流亡作家與底層歷史記錄者。2012年德國書業和平獎得主，並曾獲美國《當代基督教》雜誌頒發的「最佳圖書奬」、德國書業協會頒發的「紹爾兄妹獎」、德國廣播協會頒發的「最佳廣播劇奬」及德國阿夏芬堡頒發的「公民勇氣奬」。2013年，法國政府頒發給廖亦武「法蘭西文學藝術軍官獎章」。2018年，廖亦武獲美國紐約瓦茨拉夫 哈維爾圖書基金會頒發「無懼危難作家獎」。）http://minzhuzhongguo.org/MainArtShow.aspx?AID=105641齊家貞：《我認識的劉懷昭和魏京生》(by Qi JIazhen, writer in exile, author of autobiographical series: Tears of the Goddess of Liberty and Red Dog. Qi is the Chairwoman of the Women Writers committee, Independent Chinese PEN Center.)（作者/齊家貞，流亡作家，著有系列傳記《自由神的眼泪──父女两代囚徒的真實故事》（後改名《黑牆裡的倖存者》和《紅狗：—個被釋女囚的真實故事》在香港和台灣出版。齊家貞曾先後擔任國際筆會獨立中文筆會理事會理事、副會長、秘書長等職務，並在澳洲建立了“齊氏文化基金

# 德国前情报局长汉宁涉泄密案 被指与中国退役少将多年保持联系

茉莉花综合报道 2026年10月10日 02:23

德国联邦检察院说，德国联邦情报局前局长汉宁（August Hanning）曾与一名外国情报机构人员密切往来，多年向其提供政治信息，部分信息来自其前办公室主任交给汉宁的文件，但检察院没有说是哪个国家。有报道说，汉宁多年来与中国退役少将Wang Jianzheng保持联系（未经证实）。

80岁的汉宁1998年至2005年任德国联邦情报局局长，10月6日和其前办公室主任曼弗雷德·D.一起被捕。受这起案件直接影响的是德国联邦情报局：检方说，曼弗雷德在汉宁离职后多年为其弄到情报局领导层的机密文件，截至2022年6月共约2000份。检方还说，两人2010年达成协议，曼弗雷德向汉宁提供情报资料并收取报酬，汉宁涉嫌用这些情报为自己的私人咨询业务赚钱。

Wang Jianzheng 1987年至1990年在中国驻东柏林的代表机构工作，后来又以武官身份回到德国，是德国问题专家，翻译过多本德文书。汉宁离职后多次去中国；2017年出版的一本Wang Jianzheng与德国前总理施罗德的对话录里，Wang Jianzheng感谢汉宁给了提示和解释。两人2017年在华东城市淮北的一个招待会上见过面，2023年还同时出现在一个欧中会议的参会名单上，也都是青岛一个中德生态园顾问委员会的成员。Wang Jianzheng对媒体说，不能就指控发表评论，而且已经很久没有和汉宁联系。

联邦检察院没有说汉宁和Wang Jianzheng的关系是不是调查的一部分。汉宁的律师克鲁泽说，汉宁确实持有机密文件，但从没有在损害德国利益的情况下把其中的信息交给别人，更没有收钱。

汉宁案的几个时间点

1.   1998年至2005年 汉宁任德国联邦情报局局长
2.   2010年 检方说，汉宁和曼弗雷德达成提供情报资料的协议
3.   2022年6月 检方说，曼弗雷德到这时共向汉宁提供约2000份文件
4.   2026年10月6日 汉宁和曼弗雷德被捕

数据：德国联邦检察院、8视界新闻网、t-online

## 茉莉花观察

title: 雙十海外華媒訪臺 深化全球連結 見證臺灣民主
summary: 【大紀元2026年10月09日訊】（大紀元記者倪爾森／安平雅台灣台北報導）為迎接中華民國115年雙十國慶，僑務委員會舉辦「2026年海外華文媒體人士訪問團」，邀請來自美國、加拿大、澳洲、德國、英國、巴西、南非及菲律賓等8個國家，共19位海外華文媒體負責人、資深採訪主管與新媒體經營者返臺參訪。 [![Image 1](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14866672-PXL_20261004_101112502
content:
【大紀元2026年10月09日訊】（大紀元記者倪爾森／安平雅台灣台北報導）為迎接中華民國115年雙十國慶，僑務委員會舉辦「2026年海外華文媒體人士訪問團」，邀請來自美國、加拿大、澳洲、德國、英國、巴西、南非及菲律賓等8個國家，共19位海外華文媒體負責人、資深採訪主管與新媒體經營者返臺參訪。

[![Image 1](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14866672-PXL_20261004_101112502_3-600x400.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14866672-PXL_20261004_101112502_3.jpg)

2026年10月4日晚間歡迎餐會，時任僑委會委員長徐佳青贈送每位團員「三合一團結包」，由媒體代表團李著華團長接受。（倪爾森／大紀元）

訪問團4日晚間在臺北格萊天漾大飯店出席歡迎餐會暨委員長聯訪，5日上午拜會僑委會，聽取最新僑務政策說明。時任委員長徐佳青與副委員長李妍慧表示，期盼媒體朋友把臺灣的實況與政策帶回僑居地，協助宣傳。

## **歡迎餐會禮品融入臺灣意象**

4日晚間歡迎餐會，時任僑委會委員長徐佳青為每位團員準備了精心設計的禮品「三合一團結包」，團結包特別採用「綠、藍、白」三色搭配，象徵跨黨派攜手守護臺灣，「國家只有一個，是我們自己的。」

「團結包」內有可愛的臺灣黑熊玩偶，黑熊胸前有標誌性的白色 V 字斑紋、頭戴原住民傳統幾何圖騰頭飾與羽毛。

禮品袋設計兼具實用性與在地性，將臺灣意象、豐富的原民文化與官方識別巧妙地融合在一起，展現了臺灣的多元文化與臺灣人的熱情，是外交或海外僑界交流活動的極佳小禮品。

## **海外華媒是臺灣的眼睛與耳朵**

徐佳青致詞時代表政府，向不遠千里赴臺的媒體代表表達歡迎與感謝。她指出，海外華文媒體在世界各地深耕，不僅串聯在地僑社與臺灣的情感，更是臺灣走向世界的「眼睛」與「耳朵」。

她並回顧過往派駐溫哥華的經驗，深感臺灣在海外發聲不易，主流媒體的接觸門檻也高，因此海外華媒的傳播力量格外重要，是臺灣政府捍衛民主自由、傳遞真實訊息最值得信賴的夥伴。

面對數位科技演進與人工智慧（AI）浪潮，徐佳青強調，民主陣營正面臨假訊息與錯誤資訊的嚴峻挑戰。僑委會近年推動「6+1」全方位社群傳播模式，整合Facebook、Instagram、X、LINE@、YouTube與官方網站等六大管道，再以「愛僑卡（i僑卡）」電子郵件系統作為備援，藉由多元管道增強資訊韌性，避免信息傳播在遭受外部干擾時斷鏈，讓真實透明的聲音能穿透國際社會。

## **立足臺灣走向世界****華語教育打「國際盃」大聯盟**

談到近年在歐美等地積極拓展的「臺灣華語文學習中心」（TCML），徐佳青表示，中心不只是語言教學，更是在全球走向極端化的浪潮中，打造跨文化、跨族群、跨宗教的對話平臺。

臺灣的華語文教學堅持正體字的美學與邏輯深度，同時順應海外教學實務採用雙語（Bilingual）及拉丁字母（Alphabet）拼音模式，降低學習門檻，並導入最新研發的AI教學系統。

她說：「我們打的是『國際盃』，要做就做大聯盟，不跟特定專制政權在紅海裡打區域盃或削價競爭。」

## **解密臺灣供應鏈優勢****生態系互信如同「夜市哲學」**

在聯訪中，徐佳青也剖析臺灣在全球科技版圖與供應鏈中的獨特地位。她以臺灣夜市比喻產業生態系：攤商各司其職，賣臭豆腐、蚵仔煎或麵線的各展所長、不惡性競爭，卻能彼此串聯，形成完整且物美價廉的服務網絡。

她說，臺灣中小企業與半導體供應鏈同樣具備高度垂直分工、共存共益的精神，以及數十年累積的強大互信，「你少賺一點、我退讓一步，共同撐過景氣難關」的文化，讓臺灣產業經歷多次全球經濟風暴，仍屹立不搖。

徐佳青提到，美國IC設計大廠推動AI革命，以及輝達執行長黃仁勳多次走訪臺灣夜市，傳遞的正是同一項核心價值：唯有臺灣擁有兼具彈性、互信與高良率的民主供應鏈。

## **僑委會座談：說明最新政策、請媒體協助宣傳**

5日上午，訪問團一行拜會僑委會。副委員長李妍慧與綜合規劃處、僑民處、僑教處、僑商處、僑生處及僑務通訊社主管出席座談。李妍慧表示，國慶僑胞報到本週展開，僑委會上下動員迎接大批返國僑胞。她感謝各媒體長期在海外傳播自由、民主與多元的聲音，也讓臺灣民眾透過報導了解僑胞的想法與關切。

她指出，僑委會近年的工作重點有所調整：僑民工作轉向年輕世代，僑商工作加強新創連結與臺商、僑商對接，僑教的TCML已進入第二期計畫。

李妍慧透露，今年僑委會預算增幅相當大，若立法院順利通過，將投入更多資源吸引僑生來臺就學，並與人口政策及人才培育、留用政策結合。

訪問團團長、《芝加哥時報》總裁李著華代表訪問團致詞，感謝僑委會安排行程，讓海外媒體人親眼見證臺灣現況，盼團員把所見所聞帶回僑居地，讓僑胞了解臺灣的發展。

僑生處副處長吳曉竹說明，僑生政策已推行70年，畢業校友逾17萬人。近年配合國家人才政策，往前擴大招生，往後鼓勵留臺就業。與教育部合作的技職僑生專班，每年招生約5000至7000人；符合資格的優秀僑生，四年最高可領新臺幣156萬元獎學金。

今年1月1日起兩項法規鬆綁：僑外生畢業後可延長居留兩年，期間不需要工作許可證亦可工作；大學以上學歷也可折抵申請永久居留的年限。僑委會另提供僑生保險，補助學校聘用懂東南亞語的生活輔導員，並辦理就業博覽會與「僑生i就業」平臺，連結僑生與企業。

[![Image 2](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14866670-PXL_20261005_040742748-600x338.jpg)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14866670-PXL_20261005_040742748.jpg)

2026年10月5日海外華文媒體訪問團一行拜會僑委會，聽取各處會報告，會後由時任副委員長李妍慧，贈送禮物予代表團，由李著華團長代表接受。（倪爾森／大紀元）

僑民處處長陳永豐表示，全球已成立122個急難救助協會，今年與國防部全民防衛動員署合作，在美國9個地區巡迴辦理防災講座，明年將擴及加拿大。

為接軌僑社第二代、第三代青年，僑委會9月11日在西雅圖首次舉辦「Taiwan Night」，明年將擴大規模。

另依行政院核定的「一中心一亮點」計畫，僑教中心將在2030年前分階段優化，今年先從舊金山灣區（矽谷科技）、華府（民主人權）及休士頓（太空衛星）著手，預計明年10月前後陸續完工。

僑教處副處長陳柏琴指出，全球目前有93所TCML，招收18歲以上的主流人士，部分中心並與當地企業、市政府及圖書館合作開課。

今年的全球僑校學生暨僑生歌唱大賽，首度安排國語、臺語、客家語冠軍在國慶晚會合唱組曲，海華文教基金會選出的13位師鐸獎得主也將同臺。

僑商處專門委員王盈蓉表示，僑委會結合全球僑臺商組織促進經貿交流，舉辦青商潛力之星選拔、技術人才培訓與產業邀訪團，並透過海外信用保證基金協助企業取得融資。今年的美食巡迴講座首度結合華語文學習，各地僑商會也在棒球場、體育館等場地舉辦「臺灣日」活動。

綜合規劃處專門委員劉俊男呼籲媒體協助宣傳十月慶典線上報名，凡已歸化當地國籍的海外華人皆可參加。他也說，今年「臺灣青年海外搭僑計畫」派出82名青年赴7個地區交流，盼各地媒體多加報導。

僑務通訊社總編輯羅蓉則表示，《僑新聞》今年改版，新增中央社稿源、TaiwanPlus英文內容及公視影音，也歡迎媒體加入新聞志工行列，並可透過通訊社跨區宣傳僑社活動。

## **七天行程：產業、民主人權與國慶盛典**

僑務通訊社指出，訪問團行程自10月4日至10月10日，共七天。團員將拜會國家發展委員會、全球動力科技及龍華科技大學特色場域研發中心，了解政府推動的「五大信賴產業」與產學研合作；走訪中央通訊社與公共電視臺，交流國際傳播布局、新興媒體素養與假訊息防制；並參訪國家檔案館解嚴檔案特展、中正紀念堂「自由花蕊」常設展、國家人權博物館景美白色恐怖紀念園區，以及松山「女路走讀」與臺灣國家婦女館，完整認識臺灣由威權走向民主開放的歷程。

國慶重頭戲：訪問團將前往新北市板橋第一運動場參加雙十國慶晚會，並於10月10日國慶日當天到總統府前廣場，參加中華民國115年國慶大會。

僑委會期盼透過這次參訪，讓海外華媒以多元專業的視角，向國際社會傳遞臺灣自由民主、科技創新與包容堅韌的面貌，讓臺灣持續連結世界，也讓世界更加看見臺灣。
