content: 作者：张伟军 编辑：吕聪 皮乔海，湖北鄂州人。此前，他一直生活在洛杉矶，在洛杉矶的抗议活动中，我经常能看到他忙碌的身影。这一次，他特意乘飞机来到华盛顿特区，参加和平集会和抗议习近平活动。 9月22日，在众议院门前草坪的活动中，他扛着一口棺材，兴奋地对我说：“伟军，你看这多有趣啊！包子这口棺材，我能抬一天，十里山路不换肩都没问题！” 我笑着调侃他：“希望你有机会扛200斤小麦的时候，也能这么说。” 当时的我们，谁也没有想到，短短两天之后，这竟成了我和老乡最后一次见面前的轻松回忆。 9月23日下午，我们一同前往安德鲁斯空军基地，因为习近平当天预计最先抵达这里。 为了避免被粉红阵营巨大的旗帜遮挡，我们提前分散到几个不同的据点，包括车道左右两侧以及人行横道的三角区域。 然而，冲突还是发生了。 几名粉红看到皮乔海手中的讽刺性人像道具后，情绪激动地冲上来抢夺。双拳难敌四手，在混乱中，皮乔海胸口被中共特务特制雨伞捅伤，手指也被打出了血。 面对这一切，现场警察只是和稀泥，并没有对涉事中共特务采取任何处罚措施。这让皮乔海十分郁闷和气恼。他怎么也没有想到，在美国众目睽睽之下遭到袭击，最后竟然如此潦草收场。 9月24日，我们跟随大部队来到白宫门口参加活动。谁也没有想到，这竟然成了我和老乡最后一次见面。 活动开始前，我特意问他：“身体还好吗？” 他给我看了受伤的地方：胸口还有被雨伞捅伤留下的淤青，手指也明显肿了起来。 活动快结束时，不知道从哪里突然跑出来一群中共派来的老粉红，气势汹汹地冲过来。 按理说，当天白宫围栏外人行道的抗议活动区域是魏京生老前辈申请下来的 Permit，属于我们和平集会抗议区域，而粉红阵营在另一侧街道。这样的举动明显带有攻击目的性。 我们这边有老人、有妇女，很可能成为他们袭击的对象。皮乔海上前阻拦了一群老粉红，与其中一名粉红发生肢体冲突。这一幕恰好被一名女警察看到，他很快就被警察按倒在地。 当晚，界立健等人前往警察局了解情况。警察告诉他们，晚上12点会有结果。 漫长的等待中，终于到了午夜，传来了一喜一忧的消息。 喜的是，其他四名在混乱中被按倒在地的人都获得了释放。 悲的是，皮乔海却被指控两项罪名：殴打他人和袭警。 在美国，袭警指控可能带来严重的法律后果。据我现场所见，整场冲突中，我并没有看到皮乔海实施袭警行为。这样的指控让我们难以理解，也让人不禁质疑：事情为什么会发展到这一步？ 后来，我们又通过移民监狱网站查到了他的相关信息。 就这样，皮乔海被留在了那里，没能和我们一起踏上返程的航班。 一个为自由奔走的人，如今身陷囹圄 皮乔海为人善良、正直、谦和。他独自一人抚养着十多岁的孩子，生活十分艰难。为了维持日常生活，有时连房租都需要向朋友借钱周转。即便如此，他依然没有放弃对自由与民主的追求，始终积极参与各类和平抗议活动和捐款。 这一次，为了参加华盛顿特区的和平集会和抗议活动，他再次倾尽所能。往返交通与食宿费用共计774美元，这笔钱也是他向香港自由民主党创始人廖文浩先生借来的。 他经常提起自己的愿望：希望邪恶的独裁统治终结，希望中国能够建立一个民主、自由的社会，让普通人像台湾民众一样，不再因为表达言论、参加集会而感到恐惧，能够享有基本的人权与自由。 他说，等到那一天，他就要回到自己魂牵梦绕的家乡。 然而，如今的他却被关押在异国他乡，面对刑事指控和移民羁押的双重压力。 我很难想象，在当前移民政策和庇护审理环境下，如果他最终被遣返回中国，又将面临怎样的遭遇？ 他会不会像季超、阎友信等民运人士一样，遭遇失联，甚至从此杳无音信？ 这些担忧并非凭空而来。对于一个曾经公开表达政治观点、参加抗议活动的人来说，未来充满了太多未知。 更令人揪心的是，他在洛杉矶还有一个独自抚养的十多岁孩子。原本就十分艰难的生活，如今又因为他的被捕而蒙上了更大的阴影。 一个连房租都需要向朋友借钱、连赴华盛顿参加抗议活动的774美元都要向朋友借来的人，如今却身陷囹圄。想到这里，我的心里充满了难以言说的沉重。对于一个连房租都需要向朋友借钱的人来说，774美元绝不是一笔小数目。但他还是义无反顾地踏上了前往华盛顿的旅程，只为亲自站出来，为自由与民主发声。 我在此呼吁海外民运人士和关心中国民主、人权事业的朋友们，关注皮乔海的处境，为他提供力所能及的帮助，包括法律援助以及必要的声援。 抱薪者不可使其冻毙于风雪，仗义者不应被孤立于困境。 一个为自由奔走的人，不应该在最需要帮助的时候，被所有人遗忘。 愿皮乔海早日获得公正的对待，平安归来。

title: Mystery Shoulder-Fired Surface-To-Air Missile Appears In Russian Service
summary: An unusual shoulder-fired air defense missile seen in Russian use may be of Chinese or Iranian origin, raising questions about the movement of foreign weapons through the increasingly interconnected military supply networks linking Moscow,
content: An unusual shoulder-fired air defense missile seen in Russian use may be of Chinese or Iranian origin, raising questions about the movement of foreign weapons through the increasingly interconnected military supply networks linking Moscow, Beijing, and Tehran. The man-portable air defense system (MANPADS) appeared in Russian television footage showing a mobile air defense group operating in the Rostov region, which borders Ukraine. The weapon was shown during an exercise said to have involved one of the elements of Russia’s 51st Air Defense Division. The footage was subsequently highlighted by the X account TheDeadDistrict. ruSSian's have developed a new “Iva” MANPADS. In the footage, it is in service with one of the mobile fire groups of the 51st Air Defense Division in Rostov Oblast. Although, no—it is most likely the Iranian Misagh-2 MANPADS. Imagine, they don't even have enough production… pic.twitter.com/aYrOtSmG6h — 𝔗𝔥𝔢 𝕯𝔢𝔞𝔡 𝕯𝔦𝔰𝔱𝔯𝔦𝔠𝔱 (@TheDeadDistrict) September 28, 2026 The system does not closely resemble any of the Russian-made MANPADS families otherwise used by the country’s armed forces. Russian personnel seen with the weapon reportedly referred to it as “Iva,” although that designation by itself does not establish the weapon’s origin or model. The word Iva is Russian for willow (a type of tree), of which one particular species is named Verba — also the name of the Russian-made 9K333 MANPADS. This weapon looks very different to the example shown, but the connection is unlikely to be a coincidence. An operator of the mystery MANPADS is interviewed by the Russia-1 TV channel. Russian State Media A visual analysis of the newly observed launcher reveals comparisons with both the Iranian Misagh-3 and Chinese QW-series systems, particularly the QW-18/QW-18A and QW-19. In particular, a closer examination of the imagery highlights an additional box-like component toward the front of the launcher. That feature appears more consistent with photographs of Chinese QW-series systems rather than the Misagh. The front part of the MANPADS launcher, with the distinctive box-like component below the tub. Russian State Media There is also a scarcity of publicly available imagery of later Iranian variants to completely exclude an Iranian system. At the same time, the Misagh series itself is understood to be derived, or at least heavily influenced by Chinese designs. An Iranian Misagh-3 MANPADS with its missile. Tasnim News Agency Iranian basij with QW-18/Misagh-2 MANPADS pic.twitter.com/xfc0nMe4f8 — Yuri Lyamin (@imp_navigator) March 26, 2026 Another possibility is that the weapon is a Russian-produced version or derivative of a Chinese or Iranian design, rather than an imported system. The possibility of foreign-made or foreign-designed equipment appearing in Russian service has to be viewed against the much broader transformation of Moscow’s military relationships since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Russia’s relationship with China has deepened substantially since the invasion, with Beijing becoming a critical source of machinery, electronics, and other components that Russia’s defense industry can no longer obtain as readily from Western suppliers. Moscow and Beijing had already declared a “no limits” partnership shortly before the invasion, and their military relationship has subsequently included exercises and expanding military-technical cooperation. U.S. officials have accused China of supplying Russia with components used in weapons production, including microelectronics. Beijing has rejected accusations that it is providing lethal military assistance to Russia. A close-up of the front end of the MANPADS. Russian State Media Iran has also become an important military partner . Russia has used Iranian-designed Shahed-series attack drones extensively in Ukraine and has worked with Tehran on local production and adaptation of those systems. Moscow and Tehran formalized their relationship further with a comprehensive strategic partnership treaty in January 2025, which includes provisions for military-technical cooperation and joint exercises. In return, Russia has supplied Iran with military technology and has cooperated with Tehran on sensitive weapons programs. The possible Chinese connection takes on additional significance in light of a major reported procurement deal between China and Iran. In July, Reuters reported that Iran was expected to receive the first shipment of a deal covering 300 to 400 Chinese-made MANPADS, with a reported value of $60 million to $70 million. The weapons identified by sources included the Chinese QW-12 and FN-16 systems. Chinese missiles the United States fears… an unsleeping eye against drones and low‑flying aircraft China’s QW‑12 and FN‑16 air‑defense systems intercept low‑altitude targets — including drones — forming a rapid defensive line against close‑range aerial threats. pic.twitter.com/kJZ6mnqmHg — China Now (@ChinaNow24) August 23, 2026 The reported contract was signed with a Hong Kong-based company that sources described as an intermediary between the Iranian side and the Chinese supplier. Reuters said the initial deliveries were planned from Urumqi in western China, with the weapons then transiting through Pakistan before reaching Iran. Pakistan’s military publicly denied any involvement in such transfers, while China’s Foreign Ministry called the report “groundless.” Reuters also reported that delivery schedules and quantities could still change. More significantly for the Russian sighting, a European security source told Reuters that authorities were aware of several contracts under discussion involving the potential sale of QW-12, QW-18, and QW-19 MANPADS to Iran. A Middle Eastern security source separately claimed that Iran had been seeking QW-18 systems. The operation was carried out using a MANPADS, likely the Chinese “QW-18” anti-aircraft missile or its Iranian copy, the “Misagh-3”. https://t.co/OnPgqHJmQ8 pic.twitter.com/BuKt1MoKp7 — OSINTWarfare (@OSINTWarfare) October 23, 2024 There is currently no evidence tying the launcher seen in Russian hands to the Iranian procurement from China. At the same time, the possibility of an Iranian connection should not be ruled out, especially since Chinese-designed MANPADS have a documented history of appearing outside conventional state inventories. Earlier TWZ reporting , drawing on research by the Small Arms Survey monitoring group, examined the illicit proliferation of Chinese-designed MANPADS and identified dozens of cases involving armed groups in multiple countries. That research included QW-series weapons and documented cases in which investigators linked Chinese-designed MANPADS to Iranian supply networks. Countries with reports of illicit possession of advanced MANPADS by armed groups, 2011-21. Small Arms Survey One particularly notable case involved the Jihan , a vessel intercepted in 2013 carrying weapons that investigators identified as including QW-18-pattern MANPADS. UN investigators, the U.S. government, and   Conflict Armament Research assessed Iran as the likely source of those weapons. It is also worth noting that Chinese MANPADS have already appeared on the Ukrainian side of the war. In late 2025 and 2026, Ukrainian units were photographed with Chinese-made FN-6 and FN-16 systems, including an FN-6 associated with an air defense team reportedly engaging a Russian cruise missile. Exactly how the weapons reached Ukraine remains unclear, with possible third-party transfers or diverted shipments among the possible explanations. A Chinese FN-6 MANPADS in service with the MFG of the 143rd JTC “Podillia.” It is reported that this MANPADS was used this morning to shoot down a ruSSian Kh-101 CM. The FN-6 was developed in 2000 and supplied, among others, to Sudan, from where it likely found its way to Ukraine pic.twitter.com/9zA012ue3j — 𝔗𝔥𝔢 𝕯𝔢𝔞𝔡 𝕯𝔦𝔰𝔱𝔯𝔦𝔠𝔱 (@TheDeadDistrict) November 19, 2025 Reported as the downing of an Kh-101 cruise missile this morning using a Chinese FN-6 MANPADS. There is no public information confirming that this system has been supplied to or used by Ukraine, making this a notable development. pic.twitter.com/pUujFB81aH — NOELREPORTS (@NOELreports) November 19, 2025 Incidents like these demonstrate that Chinese MANPADS can move through indirect supply networks, including networks associated with Tehran. Regardless of how it arrived in Russia, the appearance of a foreign or foreign-derived MANPADS there is notable. Mobile fire groups have become an increasingly visible component of Russia’s layered air defense effort, particularly as the war in Ukraine has placed enormous emphasis on countering low-altitude drones and other threats, including deep inside Russia. A Russian CUAS mobile fire group shown with a Courier UGV for additional counter-drone targeting. https://t.co/7yTPPZ47f0 pic.twitter.com/bDu6MbZLEZ — Samuel Bendett (@sambendett) September 2, 2026 MANPADS are well suited to this mission because they can be dispersed among small teams, rapidly repositioned, and deployed without the larger radar and vehicle infrastructure associated with conventional surface-to-air missile batteries. In particular, they can be deployed around military installations and other sensitive infrastructure. A foreign system appearing in a Russian mobile fire group might be an imported weapon, an Iranian-produced derivative, a Chinese system acquired for evaluation, a captured weapon, or even a previously unidentified Russian configuration. model, or even that it is a brand new Chinese-made variant (its possible that I just hadn't seen it, or seen it from these angles) but it is a notable new addition to Russia's MANPADS inventory. — Matt Schroeder (@MSchroeder77) September 28, 2026 Another possibility is that the MANPADS is North Korean in origin. Russia’s military relationship with Pyongyang has expanded significantly , including the provision of increasingly advanced military equipment and technology. There is no known North Korean MANPADS matching the configuration seen here, however, and the possibility remains speculative. North Korean weapons have also frequently incorporated or closely followed Chinese designs , meaning a Chinese-looking configuration would not necessarily rule out a North Korean origin. I was able to geolocate and thus confirm that the photo of North Korean M-1978/1989 Koksan 170mm SPGs was taken in Russia. 56.069386, 92.920244 Krasnoyarsk, central Russia https://t.co/BOaR44uLeS https://t.co/mC8solXVOv pic.twitter.com/LUHO2cllKZ — Status-6 (@Archer83Able) November 14, 2024 Russia has dramatically expanded defense production since 2022, but its industry remains under heavy wartime demand and sanctions-related constraints. Western restrictions have complicated access to advanced electronics, machine tools and other components, while Russia has increasingly relied on domestic substitutes and foreign suppliers. The mystery MANPADS launchers disassembled and in a container for transport. Russian State Media At the same time, Russia must replenish weapons consumed in Ukraine, meaning foreign supplies could supplement domestic production, fill specific gaps, or allow scarce industrial capacity to be directed elsewhere. For Russia, even a limited number of additional shoulder-fired systems could therefore have practical value as Ukrainian long-range strike capabilities continue to expand. For now, the exact model and provenance of the MANPADS in question remain unconfirmed, but the apparent Chinese or Iranian design characteristics are highly noteworthy. Further appearances of the system could provide the clues needed to determine what it is, where it came from, and whether this represents an isolated example or a more significant acquisition effort. Contact the author: thomas@thewarzone.com The post Mystery Shoulder-Fired Surface-To-Air Missile Appears In Russian Service appeared first on TWZ .

title: Lai urges respect for WWII history, Taiwan's 'right to exist' - Focus Taiwan
summary: Taipei, Oct. 10 (CNA) Taiwan welcomes efforts by the United States and China to reduce the risk of war through dialogue, but the two superpowers should also respect the historical record of World War II and the Taiwanese people's right to e
content:
Taipei, Oct. 10 (CNA) Taiwan welcomes efforts by the United States and China to reduce the risk of war through dialogue, but the two superpowers should also respect the historical record of World War II and the Taiwanese people's right to exist, President Lai Ching-te (賴清德) said Saturday in his National Day address.

Faced with sustained "gray zone" pressure from China, Taiwan has increased defense spending and worked to strengthen society's overall ability to defend itself by combining government and civilian capabilities, Lai said.

Such efforts are not meant as a provocation, but to ensure dialogue can take place on the basis of "dignity and parity," he said.

"We welcome the United States and China managing their competition through dialogue and reducing the risk of conflict and war," he said. "But we must also point out that maintaining regional security, peace and stability requires a correct understanding of how history has unfolded."

"There must be no tolerance for distorting the history of World War II. There must be respect for the right of the people of Taiwan to exist," Lai said in the address, which marked the 115th anniversary of the founding of the ROC.

"We are open to exchanges, but will not accept subordination," he said.

The ROC government relocated to Taiwan from mainland China in 1949 after its defeat in the Chinese Civil War by Communist forces, which founded the People's Republic of China.

In his address, Lai also said that Taiwan is "going farther, step by step, with our diplomacy."

He cited his visit in May to Eswatini, Taiwan's sole African ally, which took place amid Chinese attempts to block the trip by pressuring three African states to deny his chartered flight access to their airspace.

He also mentioned Vice President Hsiao Bi-khim's (蕭美琴) visit to Palau, another ally of Taiwan, in June and her speech at the European Conference of Ventotene for Freedom and Democracy in Italy in September.

Taiwan has worked with its international partners on health care, agriculture, energy, technology, education and sustainable development to meet their needs, and has improved lives through those efforts, Lai said.

"'Taiwan Can Help' is not just a slogan. It is a commitment -- our willingness to share our capabilities and shoulder responsibility," he said.

Taiwan seeks international recognition despite sustained efforts by Beijing to isolate it. China claims Taiwan as part of its territory that must be unified, by force if necessary.

(By Sean Lin)

Enditem/sfj

Contact Information: Commercial Section Address: 100 Jinhu Road, Neihu District, Taipei 114017, Taiwan Tel: +886 (2) 2162-2000 Fax: +886 (2) 2162- 2159 E-Mail: office.taipei@trade.gov Bureau of Industry and Security, U.S. Department of Commerce Regional Export Control Officer (Taiwan, Japan, Korea) – Ariel Joshua Leinwand Export Control Specialist – Ann Chen BIS Export Control Officers (ECOs) play a key role in ensuring compliance with the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) outside the U.S. to prevent illicit diversion to unauthorized uses and/or destinations. These overseas BIS representatives expand the U.S. government’s export compliance capabilities beyond its borders and into key overseas trade centers. BIS currently has eleven ECOs in key locations in Taiwan, Hong Kong, PRC, Singapore, India, Germany, Finland, UAE, Turkey, and an export compliance analyst based in Canada. ECOs conduct site visits, known as End-Use Checks (EUCs), globally with end-users, consignees, and/or other parties related to transactions involving items subject to the EAR to verify compliance with the EAR. BIS officials rely on EUCs to safeguard items subject to the EAR from diversion to unauthorized end uses/users and destinations. title: Rare Earth Talks Keep US-China Supply Chain Open
summary: A key ally of Donald Trump is pushing Washington to keep talking to Beijing over rare earths, underscoring how dependent US manufacturers remain on Chinese minerals even as the two sides accuse each other of weaponizing supply chains. Steve
content:
A key ally of Donald Trump is pushing Washington to keep talking to Beijing over rare earths, underscoring how dependent US manufacturers remain on Chinese minerals even as the two sides accuse each other of weaponizing supply chains.

Steve Daines, the outgoing Montana senator and a prominent Republican China hawk, told the South China Morning Post that the answer to disputes over critical minerals was “not to retreat” but to “stay engaged,” after US ambassador to China David Perdue accused Beijing of using its “single-source dominant position” in critical minerals against the world.

Geopolitical Risk sentiment is strongly positive at 86.

The exchange matters because rare earths are no longer a narrow trade irritant: they are a strategic input into electric vehicles, defense systems, wind turbines and advanced electronics. China’s tightening export controls in 2025 made that dependence more visible, forcing companies to seek licenses and approvals even when products contain only small amounts of Chinese-origin material, according to MP Materials’ latest filing.

That leaves Washington with a difficult policy balance. On one side is the push to reduce exposure to China through domestic mining, processing and magnet production. On the other is the near-term reality that the US still lacks sufficient scale outside China to fully insulate industry from supply shocks. The result is a strong incentive for engagement even among lawmakers and officials who favor tougher competition.

*   US-China Relations

Explore this data interactively — full history, time series and cross-market comparisons.[Open AlphaPulse](https://adalytica.com/alpha-pulse)

For investors, the signal is that rare earths remain a geopolitical price-setting market, not just a commodity niche. MP Materials, which owns a rare earth metal, alloy and magnet plant in Texas, sits closest to any improvement in US policy support or supply-chain reordering, but it also remains exposed to policy-driven volatility in Chinese exports and critical mineral pricing. Albemarle, while better known for lithium, also has exposure to the broader shift in battery and strategic mineral supply chains, and the sector’s pricing has been whipsawed by changing policy expectations and Chinese controls.

The market backdrop reinforces the stakes. MP shares closed at $46.97 on Oct. 2, well below its 50-day average of about $51, while its relative strength index remained below 40, a sign of recent weakness. Taiwan chipmaker TSMC, by contrast, has traded much stronger, reflecting how investors continue to favor firms with tighter control over essential supply chains. The divergence highlights the market’s view: strategic mineral producers can benefit from policy urgency, but they remain vulnerable to political headlines and uneven execution.

The broader narrative is that US-China competition over critical materials is entering a more pragmatic phase. Even as Washington frames China’s dominance as a security risk, Republicans close to Trump appear to recognize that outright disengagement would increase costs for US industry and complicate efforts to build alternative supply chains. The likely near-term outcome is more dialogue, not less, with rare earths one of the few areas where confrontation and negotiation have to coexist.

For investors, the key question is whether engagement leads to more predictable export terms or merely postpones another disruption. Any sign of stable licensing, new bilateral understandings or fresh US industrial support could lift strategic mineral names. But if talks stall, the sector remains exposed to a renewed squeeze that would ripple through defense, autos, clean energy and semiconductor supply chains.

title: Ex-husband, in-laws accused of murdering Hong Kong model Abby Choi appear in court
summary: The ex-husband and in-laws accused of murdering Hong Kong model and influencer Abby Choi appeared in court on Wednesday, in a gruesome case that has sent shockwaves through the city. Abby Choi in 2022. Photo: Abby Choi, via Instagram. Choi,
content: The ex-husband and in-laws accused of murdering Hong Kong model and influencer Abby Choi appeared in court on Wednesday, in a gruesome case that has sent shockwaves through the city. Abby Choi in 2022. Photo: Abby Choi, via Instagram. Choi, an influencer with more than 140,000 followers on Instagram, had shared photos from Paris Fashion Week just days before she was killed in 2023. Police discovered parts of the 28-year-old’s dismembered body at a house in suburban Hong Kong. Her death was widely reported in the city, where violent crime is relatively rare. Alex Kwong, his father Kwong Kau and brother Anthony Kwong pleaded not guilty to murder charges, judge Brian Keith told a nine-person jury on Wednesday. The three defendants, who face life in prison if found guilty, appeared calm as they attended the hearing. They are also accused of preventing the lawful burial of a body, with two of them, Alex and Anthony Kwong, pleading guilty. Choi had two children with Alex Kwong, but later divorced him and married Chris Tam, with whom she had two more children. Property dispute Prosecutors told the court on Wednesday that Choi and her ex-husband’s family had financial disputes over a luxury property she had bought for them. They said they believed Choi had decided to register the property under the name of her former father-in-law years ago to avoid paying higher taxes. Prosecution lawyer Charlotte Draycott told the court that Choi’s relationship with the Kwong family began to deteriorate in 2022 after she tried to sell the luxury flat, for which she had paid HK$60 million ($7.65 million). Kadooria, the luxury property in Ho Man Tin that Abby Choi reportedly bought. Photo: Google Maps. Prosecutors said Kwong Kau, a 68-year-old retired police sergeant, had become “extremely resentful and angry” over the attempt to sell the flat. They said he decided to kill Choi because he wanted to keep the flat and that he and his sons decided to work together. “We say three of them decided they would do it together,” said Draycott, adding that each of them “played a part” in Choi’s death and burying her body in a suburban house. The trial, which adjourned until Friday, is expected to last until December.

title: The Case for Talking to China Is Not a Case for Détente
source: 芝加哥全球事务委员会
summary: The Case for Talking to China Is Not a Case for Détente ccolon Mon, 09/28/2026 - 12:21 This article was originally published by the Financial Times . This week’s US-China summit was long on symbolism and short on substance. No big deals or
content: The Case for Talking to China Is Not a Case for Détente ccolon Mon, 09/28/2026 - 12:21 This article was originally published by the Financial Times . This week’s US-China summit was long on symbolism and short on substance. No big deals or grand bargains were reached, let alone discrete deliverables. That reflects both Donald Trump’s aversion to preparation and the economic stalemate following the 2025 trade war.  Yet this summit should not be dismissed as mere spectacle. Trump hosting Xi Jinping at the White House matters. And regular leader meetings, possibly two more at multilateral gatherings this year, keep the trade truce alive and the lines of communication open.  That is needed today. Global politics is in a strategic interregnum, moving on from the era of US dominance and a rules-based order. But to what? With two regional wars raging, the range of possible geopolitical outcomes is wider today than perhaps in any period since the 1920s. What is not uncertain is the centrality of the US-China relationship.  Washington and Beijing are in the early days of a long-term competition whose terms and boundaries are still being set. As such, more communication is better than less. Summit diplomacy, properly handled, can reduce misperception, encourage restraint, narrow differences and foster co-operation. This is desperately needed in a relationship whose list of problems, from AI to Taiwan, is expanding.  This week’s summit addressed few of these issues, but it at least bought both sides more time and stability. But the case for talking is not a case for détente: a stable arrangement based on shared strategic interests. Summits are not cost-free; they allow China to play for time and project an image of comity, if not accommodation. Time and stability are only valuable if used well.  With summits like this, Washington risks sending signals that embolden Beijing rather than deter it. This is especially true on issues like Taiwan and Japan, where Trump appears receptive to Xi’s calls for restraint. US-China relations work best with clear, consistent and credible communication about American interests, backed by leverage. But Trump has his own view of US interests: criticising allies while embracing China.  Advocates of détente misunderstand both the state of US-China relations today and Xi’s global aspirations. Ties between the two countries today rest on a fragile truce, agreed in autumn 2025 to pause the trade war. It is underpinned by mutual economic vulnerability: both can inflict serious damage on the other. Washington and Beijing both value the stability of a truce, but both are racing to reduce their vulnerability and increase their leverage. For China that means reducing exposure to US tariffs and technology controls; for the US, reducing dependence on rare earths and magnets.  Some now argue that this mutual economic vulnerability can do for Washington and Beijing what nuclear deterrence did in the cold war. That would be a dangerous mistake.    The inherent instability of the cold war’s mutually assured destruction (MAD) is often forgotten. Washington and Moscow constantly tried to escape MAD, often with risky military operations. Nuclear vulnerability was hard to escape. Economic vulnerability is far less so. Today’s stalemate—built on narrow economic vulnerabilities—is not an equilibrium. It is a race, and summits set its pace, but aren’t a finish line.   Today’s bilateral bargaining is also lopsided. China’s actions, such as pauses on export controls and soyabean purchases, can be reversed overnight. American concessions on technology cannot. China’s economic challenges explain why Xi wants calm now, but that is a reason to buy time, not to settle.  Meanwhile, strategic competition persists. Both sides are putting each other’s companies on control lists and denying access to critical technologies. China’s military coercion in Asia is intensifying, as is its support for Russia’s war in Ukraine and for Iran. No one knows where the boundaries are, until they are crossed. The summit clarified none of this and, worryingly, projected the image of a US-China “G2” condominium. That image matters all over the world but especially in Asia. Coexistence in the cold war rested not on summits and restraint alone, but on alliances and military capabilities. Détente without credible deterrence is not the basis for coexistence; instead, it invites miscalculation and instability. Trump’s affinity for Xi and dealmaking with China are also at odds with hawks in his own administration and Congress, undermining its political sustainability at home and credibility abroad.   Xi believes the US is accelerating its own decline but remains dangerous because it could lash out on the way down. His plan is not to confront Washington but to accumulate power and influence until a transition becomes inevitable. Xi needs time to make China less reliant on others and others more reliant on it, beginning with the US.  So, the real question arising from the summit is who will make better use of the breathing room it has created. Washington should use it to build alternative supply chains, align export controls with partners, rebuild its force posture, reassure Taipei, Tokyo and Manila, and insist on crisis communications that work. If Washington treats the summit as an achievement in and of itself rather than an opportunity to do more, then it has already lost the competition. title: BigBang throws concert in Taipei; Jay Chou shares photos with group - Focus Taiwan
summary: Taipei, Oct. 10 (CNA) South Korean boy band BigBang performed in Taiwan for the first time in 11 years on Friday night, drawing 40,000 fans to Taipei Dome to welcome the group's three members -- G-Dragon (GD), Taeyang and Daesung. Mandopop
content:
Taipei, Oct. 10 (CNA) South Korean boy band BigBang performed in Taiwan for the first time in 11 years on Friday night, drawing 40,000 fans to Taipei Dome to welcome the group's three members -- G-Dragon (GD), Taeyang and Daesung.

Mandopop star Jay Chou (周杰倫) shared photos of himself with the K-pop group on Instagram, writing, "Nice to see you guys! Congratulations." The post prompted netizens to respond with praise, with some describing the photos as "dream group photos."

BigBang kicked off the concert with its signature song "Fantastic Baby" as the 40,000 fans at the venue waved their hands and screamed with excitement. The music video for the song, released in 2012, has garnered 670 million views on YouTube.

The group subsequently performed other popular songs, including "Hands Up," "Tonight," "Blue" and "Loser," to the delight of fans.

During "Tonight," GD even recreated his signature guitar-smashing scene at the end of the song.

On stage, GD spoke Mandarin to the audience, saying, "Long time no see. How have you been? I'm Big Brother Dragon." He added, "I miss you all."

Taeyang spoke Taiwanese, telling the crowd, "I love you all. I am Taeyang," prompting loud screams from the audience.

Taeyang said Taipei was the first Asian stop on BigBang's world tour.

He added that after arriving in Taiwan on Thursday night, he enjoyed his' favorite Taiwanese foods, including beef noodle soup and pineapple cakes. He also praised BigBang's fans for being sweet and warm.

In addition to performing as a group, the three BigBang members also sang solo.

At one point, Taeyang slipped on two steps while leaving the stage, but quickly grabbed the handrail to avoid falling. After stepping off the stage, he warmly held a fan's hand as the performance continued, much to the delight of the audience.

After the concert, Chou posed for photos with BigBang beside a flower basket he had sent to the group. Some netizens commented that Chou and BigBang had been part of their childhood, describing them as superstars who transcend generations.

BigBang will hold two more concerts at Taipei Dome on Saturday and Sunday as part of its "BigBang 2026-2027 World Tour XX:Cosmos in Taipei," celebrating the group's 20th anniversary.

A woman surnamed Lau (劉), who flew from Hong Kong to Taipei, told CNA on Thursday that she had taken two days off work to attend two of BigBang's concerts in Taipei. She said she enjoyed attending concerts in Taiwan because local fans were friendlier and the overall atmosphere was more harmonious, making the concert experience even better.

(By Wang Hsin-yu, Wu Jui-chi and Frances Huang)

content: 最新消息：英国民众们最熟悉的招牌之一美妆、药店Boots，正式找到了新主人。 买家是加拿大的韦斯顿家族（Weston family）。 他们通过旗下投资公司Wittington Investments出手，交易对Boots的估值约为67亿英镑（含债务），折合约89亿美元。 韦斯顿这个名字，很多中国读者未必熟悉。 可他们家的品牌，几乎人人都逛过。 1.一家草药店的177年 Boots的故事要从1849年说起。 那一年，诺丁汉开了一家小小的家庭草药店。 谁也没想到，这家店后来会成长为英国最大的药妆连锁。 今天的Boots，在英国有超过1,800家门店，员工超过5.1万人。 英国和爱尔兰的门店加起来约2,000家。会员卡活跃用户超过1,700万。 它还是英国国家医疗服务体系NHS药房服务的主要提供方之一。 截至2025年8月的财年，Boots营收75亿英镑，增长3.2%。税前利润3.37亿英镑，增长25%。新引进的美妆品牌和减肥针需求，是两大推手。 生意好，日子却不太安稳。 过去十几年，Boots一直在资本之间辗转。 2.被反复转手的老牌药店 2012年，美国连锁药店Walgreens入股Boots，后来两家合并成了Walgreens Boots Alliance。 2022年，Walgreens曾想把Boots单独卖掉，私募巨头Apollo和TDR Capital都来看过。 出价达不到预期，交易最终告吹。 2025年8月，私募基金Sycamore Partners以237亿美元（含债务）把Walgreens Boots Alliance整体私有化。 随后，它把集团拆成五家独立公司，Boots是其中之一。 原掌门人Stefano Pessina的家族，在这五家公司里各保留约44%的股份。 摆在Sycamore面前的，有两条路。一条是卖掉，一条是上市。 今年4月，有消息称Boots在为最早2027年伦敦上市做准备。5月，Boots请来了前Currys执行官Alex Baldock。 他在Currys主导的扭亏广受好评，市场普遍把这次任命看作上市前的铺垫。9月2日，他正式上任。 3.一场讨价还价的拉锯战 真正的好戏，发生在谈判桌上。 据报道，复活节前Sycamore就开始和潜在买家接触。 6月，《金融时报》披露，韦斯顿家族和澳大利亚药房集团Sigma Healthcare都在谈，交易规模约100亿美元，折合约75亿英镑。 同样在6月，Sigma退出了竞购。 韦斯顿家族发现自己成了唯一的买家，随即压低了出价。 一位知情人士对《每日电讯报》说得很直白： 对方意识到自己是“唯一的玩家”，就想砍价。 8月，Sycamore拒绝了这个更低的报价，谈判陷入僵局。当时的说法是，成交概率只有五五开。 到了9月，市场逐渐平静，双方又回到谈判桌。据报道，最终价格更接近韦斯顿家族的报价。 从年中传出的75亿英镑，到最后的67亿英镑，中间差了约8亿英镑。 对Sycamore来说，买下来一年多就脱手，依然是一次漂亮的退出。 伦敦股市则少了一宗近十年规模最大的英国零售业上市之一。 4.韦斯顿家族是什么来头 韦斯顿家族横跨英国和加拿大，分成两支。 英国这一支控股Associated British Foods，简称ABF。 Primark就是它旗下的品牌，川宁茶Twinings和Ryvita饼干也是。 伦敦皮卡迪利大街上的老牌百货Fortnum & Mason，同样属于这个家族。ABF今年已经确认，计划把Primark拆分独立上市，目标在2027年底前完成。 这次买下Boots的，是加拿大那一支，由Galen Weston掌舵。 他们手里有加拿大最大的食品杂货零售商Loblaw，还有连锁药妆店Shoppers Drug Mart。后者在加拿大有超过1,300家门店，同样把药房、美妆和日用品放在一个屋檐下。 说白了，这就是加拿大版的Boots。 这一支和英国零售业还有一段旧缘。 他们曾拥有伦敦的Selfridges百货近二十年，2022年以40亿英镑卖给了泰国Central Group和奥地利Signa。 这一次，算是带着重金回归英国高街。 5.大品牌租客为什么让房东安心 讲完家族故事，回到投资者最关心的问题：这和商业地产有什么关系？ Boots在英国有1,800多家门店，背后是成百上千位房东。租客换了老板，房东最在意的是两件事：租金还能不能按时交，租约还能不能续。 英国商铺投资里有一个核心概念，叫租客信誉（tenant covenant）。 同一间铺子，租给一家小店和租给一家全国连锁，估值可能差出很多。 道理很简单，大品牌更可能长期稳定地付租。 这次接手Boots的，是经营零售上百年的家族，自己本身就在做同类生意。 对房东来说，这是一个让人放心的信号。 英国的商铺租约，和住宅很不一样。常见的是FRI租约，也就是全修缮全保险租约。房屋的维修和保险费用大多由租客承担，房东拿到的接近净租金。 租期也比住宅长得多，五年、十年甚至更长都很常见。 看一份商铺租约，有几处要特别留意。 先看租客是谁，要查到具体签约的公司，看有没有母公司担保。 再看剩余租期有多长。租期越短，续约风险越大。 还要看有没有提前解约条款（Break clause），什么时候可以行使。 租金复核怎么约定，是只升不降，还是按市场租金调整，这一点尤其关键。 英国高街过去几年经历过租金重新定价，一些老租约到期续签时，租金会明显回落。 所以买商铺不能只看当前租金和表面回报率，还要判断这个租金放在今天的市场里是否合理。 6.这笔交易给海外买家的启发 一家连锁药店的买卖，背后的道理放在住宅市场同样适用。 好位置永远稀缺。资本可以几易其手，开在人流核心地段的门店，价值却很难被替代。 零售园区可用面积只剩1.8%，租金上涨了四分之一，零售商依然抢着续租，说到底就是物以稀为贵。 住宅市场也是一样。交通便利、配套成熟、靠近就业和名校的房子，供应有限，需求却一直都在。 伦敦、曼彻斯特、伯明翰这些大城市的核心区域，土地本就稀缺，好房源更是可遇不可求。 好租客和好地段往往相伴而来。 大品牌愿意长期留在好位置，优质租客同样愿意为好地段的房子支付稳定的租金。对购房出租的海外买家来说，地段决定了租客的质量，也决定了出租房的空置风险。 一家诺丁汉的小草药店，走过177年，换过好几任主人，依然站在英国高街的中央。 零售的形态一直在变，买房的形态也一直在变，人们对好地段的追求，始终没变。

Our family is heartbroken by the devastating floods that swept through communities along the Nepal–Tibet border, destroying homes, livelihoods, and taking many precious lives—including our beloved first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa Dakpu Lama Tamang.

Who We Are & Our Connection

We are Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering, and members of the Gangshar family whose roots are deeply connected to the communities affected by this tragedy. We are raising these funds for our first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and their two young children, who are now facing an unimaginable loss and an uncertain future.

“Cho Cho” is an endearing Tibetan term for an older brother. To our family, Cho Cho Dawa was a beloved husband, father, son, brother, nephew, cousin, and friend.

A Father Who Gave Everything for His Family

At 45 years old, Cho Cho Dawa worked as a mountain guide in Nepal’s Langtang region, providing for his wife and two children. His work often took him away from home for weeks or months at a time, but he took great pride in what he did. He was known for his warmth, kindness, generosity, and joyful spirit.

Tragically, the mountains he knew so well and worked in to support his family became the place where he lost his life.

He leaves behind his wife and two young children—a daughter, 11, and a son, 7. They are now facing not only the devastating loss of their husband and father, but the uncertainty of rebuilding their lives without the person who provided for their family.

The picture attached captures Cho Cho Dawa with his family dressed in our traditional Tibetan attire while celebrating Losar, the Tibetan New Year.

Our Family’s Connection to This Community

Our connection to this region goes back generations.

Our father and his family originally came from Kyidong (Kyirong, སྐྱིད་གྲོང་) in Tibet, a place now often referred to as Gyirong in international news. In 1959, our grandparents and relatives were forced to flee Tibet and eventually found refuge and a new home in the border regions of Nepal.

Our father and his siblings grew up in the Syabru besi and Briddhim communities, where they went to school, formed lifelong friendships, and began rebuilding their lives after leaving Tibet. These communities became an important part of our family’s history and home in Nepal.

The school where our father and his siblings once studied was among the places devastated by the floods.

Yangkey was fortunate to visit Syabru besi and Briddhim in March 2014 and again with Choenyi in November 2025. During those visits, she spent time with Cho Cho Dawa, his wife, mother, and brother and was warmly welcomed into their home. The pictures included here were taken during those visits and are now incredibly meaningful to our family.

The pictures also show places we saw and experienced during our November 2025 visit. One shows a hydropower facility along the road to Syabru besi which has been damanged and another shows the homes, guesthouses, and local businesses in Syabru besi, many of which have since been washed away.

Our family was once forced to leave our homeland in Tibet and found a place in Nepal where generations of our family could rebuild their lives. Now, that same community has been devastated by another unimaginable tragedy.

What took generations to build was swept away in moments. But the lives, memories, and stories connected to these places remain.

We Are Grieving Many Losses

Cho Cho Dawa is not the only loss our family is mourning.

His brother, Cho Cho Tsering, is also facing unimaginable grief, as members of his wife’s family were among those tragically swept away.

We are also mourning the many precious lives lost in this devastating tragedy, including relatives, friends, and members of the Tibetan community.

Behind every life lost is a family now facing a future without someone they love.

How the Funds Will Be Used

We are raising funds to directly support Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and two children as they begin rebuilding their lives without him.

The funds will be used specifically for:

*   Food and daily necessities
*   Shelter, rent, and household expenses
*   Clothing and essential supplies
*   School-related expenses and future education costs for the children
*   Medical and other essential family needs that may arise
*   Long-term support to help the family regain stability and rebuild their lives

100% of the funds raised through this GoFundMe will go directly toward supporting Cho Cho Dawa’s family and, if we are fortunate enough to raise more than is needed for Cho Cho Dawa’s immediate family, additional funds will be used to help other affected families in the Tibetan community of Syabru besi who have lost loved ones, homes, or their livelihoods as a result of this disaster.

Bringing the Help Directly to Nepal

Yangkey will be traveling to Nepal in approximately two weeks and plans to personally deliver the funds raised directly to the affected families. The funds will be used solely for the relief, essential needs, and family-support purposes described above.

We want to make sure the support reaches those who need it most and provides meaningful help during this incredibly difficult time.

Every donation, no matter the amount, can make a meaningful difference.

If you are unable to donate, please consider sharing this fundraiser with your friends, family, coworkers, and community. A share may help this story reach someone who is able to help.

Thank you for taking the time to hear Cho Cho Dawa’s story and for standing with his wife and children, our family, and the communities affected by this devastating tragedy.

From our family to yours, thank you for your kindness, compassion, love, and support.

With gratitude,

Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering & Gangshar Family

By [Sebastian Strangio](https://thediplomat.com/authors/sebastian-strangio/)

October 06, 2026

Laos’ National Assembly yesterday approved a major leadership change that included the removal of Prime Minister Sonexay Siphandone.

In what the state-run Vientiane Times [described](https://www.vientianetimes.org.la/freefreenews/freecontent_192_NA_y26.php) as “a significant change in senior state leadership,” lawmakers yesterday voted unanimously to appoint Sonexay’s deputy Saleumxay Kommasith as the country’s new prime minister. Sonexay was appointed president of the National Assembly, succeeding the late Xaysomphone Phomvihane.

The position has been vacant since Xaysomphone, the son of revered communist leader Kaysone Phomvihane, [died in August](https://asianews.network/laos-national-assembly-president-xaysomphone-phomvihane-dies-at-age-70/) at the age of 70. The Central Committee of the ruling Lao People’s Revolutionary Party [described](https://asianews.network/laos-national-assembly-president-xaysomphone-phomvihane-dies-at-age-70/) his passing as “an immense loss for the Party, the State and the Lao people of all ethnic groups.”

According to [the Laotian Times](https://laotiantimes.com/2026/10/05/saleumxay-kommasith-becomes-laos-new-prime-minister-sonexay-takes-national-assembly-helm/?fbclid=IwY2xjawUxChhleHRuA2FlbQIxMABwZG9mAWJyaWQRMTZDVUdWU0NpR09aZnoxd3BzcnRjBmFwcF9pZBAyMjIwMzkxNzg4MjAwODkyAAEeuQXa8vhzBU9Y1Z_tZceSYVO727MGarMhv324QrvHsDvEzox2ykeu2j6Hhhs_aem_F4pZSewX_dfnxPsBKPhxTQ), 57-year-old Saleumxay has a background in diplomacy, having spent much of his career in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. He has previously served as Laos’ representative to the United Nations and as foreign minister between 2016 and 2024, and was also appointed as a deputy prime minister in 2022.

Beyond the need to fill the vacant National Assembly position, Lao media reports were reticent about the reasons for Sonexay’s removal, and in Laos it is often hard to separate performance-based from patronage-based appointments. content:
也门政府星期一(10月5日)说，在也门领导人星期日宣布对伊朗支持的胡塞武装发动大规模攻势后，也门军队已经重新夺回了俯瞰战略要道曼德海峡能源要道的领土。

也门政府星期一(10月5日)表示，在也门领导人星期日宣布对伊朗支持的胡塞武装发动大规模攻势后，也门军队已收复战略性红海港口城市摩查(Al-Mocha)，以及俯瞰战略要道曼德海峡能源要道的领土。

美国国务卿马尔科·卢比奥(Marco Rubio)星期一对记者说，也门军队努力夺回在最近一次攻势中被胡塞武装占领的地区。卢比奥还说，一直遭受胡塞武装导弹和无人机猛烈袭击的沙特阿拉伯，有权对这些袭击进行防御。

也门国家通讯社莎巴通讯社(Saba News Agency)在X上发布的一篇报道指出，政府军和盟军在星期一与胡塞武装的激烈战斗后，控制了泰伊兹(Taiz)省西部的摩查。报道称，部队在空中支援下夺取了这座城市。

**联军行动**

也门总统领导委员会主席拉沙德·穆罕默德·阿利米(Rashad Muhammad Al-Alimi)星期日宣布启动“也门黎明”行动，他说行动目标是恢复国家机构，并收复首都萨那。

也门军方发言人马吉德·努扎伊利(Majed Al-Nuzaili)上校报告，多条战线星期日以来都有军事行动，并称亲政府武装民兵在西南战线的杜巴布(Dhubab)地区取得了进展。

努扎伊利在X上贴文说，“巨人旅(Giants Forces)和国民之盾(National Shield)部队成功控制了曼德海峡。杜巴布机场已由政府军控制。”

他说，他们的部队切断了杜巴布与主要港口城市摩查之间的道路，并正在巩固控制。

努扎伊利说，政府军还对胡塞武装2014年占领的首都萨那开展了“战略进攻行动”。

沙特阿拉伯领导的联盟包括埃及、约旦、巴林、科威特和马来西亚等支持国际承认的也门政府的国家。联盟说，共有100架战斗机参与了此次行动，为地面部队提供空中支援。

联盟发言人图尔基·马尔基(Turki al-Malki)少将表示，联盟摧毁了324个高价值目标，并确保海峡的空中保护。

**胡塞武装的宣称**

在之前否认也门政府军取得领土进展之后，胡塞武装控制的媒体确认了在杜巴布郊区发生的战斗。

胡塞叛军还声称，沙特空袭在也门萨那省造成9人死亡。胡塞军事发言人亚哈·萨里(Yahya Saree)在X平台上发布帖文称，他们在泰伊兹省击落了一架沙特侦察无人机。

这个美国认定的恐怖组织声称已将沙特支持的部队从泰伊兹省的马瓦西特(Mawasit)区驱逐出去，并抵达了总统领导委员会主席阿利米(Al-Alimi)的住所。

胡塞武装星期一还声称，沙特空袭在萨那省造成九人死亡，包括一名女学生，但这些伤亡情况尚未得到独立核实。

**美国反应**

当被问及沙特支持的也门军队发起的攻势时，卢比奥国务卿星期一说，利雅得遭到了胡塞武装的袭击，并指出“他们有权自卫”。

“很显然，也门军队将会试图夺回他们被驱逐出去的领土，”他在前往冰岛之前在安德鲁斯联合基地对记者说。

据X上的一个贴文说，美国驻也门临时代办尼尔·霍普(Neil Hop)星期日会见了也门外交部长阿夫拉赫·祖巴(Afrah Al-Zouba)，讨论了胡塞武装对红海航行自由的威胁以及在泰伊兹对平民发动的袭击。

霍普说，“美国与也门合法政府站在一起，努力对抗伊朗支持的胡塞武装。”

美国和联合国官员警告称，胡塞武装上个月的推进可能会扰乱曼德海峡和红海的海上航运，这个组织公开表示将继续攻击沙特阿拉伯的船只。

联合国上星期报告，也门正在出现饥饿问题，在该国能进入地区接受调查的家庭中，近四分之三的家庭无法满足其基本食物需求。联合国警告说，也门的粮食不安全状况正在加剧，持续的战斗扰乱了市场，限制了人道援助的进入。

title: 顏純鈎：新聞工作者是政府天敵，揭社會真相是記者天職

content: 作者臉書 2026-10-4 今年9月中，特朗普政府宣佈禁止三家美國主流媒體進入白宮採訪，指控他們長期傳播假消息。此事引起美國媒體全面反彈，超過五十家傳媒聯名抵制，五大電視網一度暫停白宮聯合採訪以示抗議。 此後，三家被禁媒體即入禀法院控告政府違憲，聯邦法院法官裁定白宮禁令無效，下令白宮立即歸還記者通行證，並頒臨時禁制令。但政府並未因此罷手，9月底再度無預警將CNN剔出總統隨行記者團及「空軍一號」採訪名單。 此事顯示特朗普是一個氣量狹窄又濫用職權的總統，但他在發洩對媒體不滿情緒的同時，也蒙受政府政策和活動報道不足的負面影響，對政府的公關有損無益。 在美國，媒體有法律保障的獨立性，不受政府好惡干擾，在這件事情上，顯示美國司法獨立的重要性，凡是朝野爭執，最後總有司法部門依法裁決，誰都不能一手遮天。 美國媒體對堅持新聞採訪的合法權利，也堅持統一的立場，不會因為媒體之間有競爭關係，便樂見敵對傳媒遭遇不公平待遇，趁機擴大自己的版圖，而是站在統一立場對抗政府，因為媒體本就是政府天敵，民主國家自由媒體，就是為公眾利益而生。 與此同時，在香港也發生一件政府壓制媒體的事件。網媒「爆炸頭」創辦人鄧浩榮，被指直播「831」太子站襲擊事件七周年，被國安處便衣帶走。香港記者協會發表聲明，對此事深表關切。記協認為直播如實報道現場發生事態，在公眾地方記錄及直播現況，是基本新聞工作，得到相關法律保障，政府應尊重新聞及言論自由，並確保鄧浩榮能及時獲得法律代表。 自國安法凌駕香港以來，政府便視自由媒體為敵對勢力，紙媒停刊的停刊，轉向的轉向，網媒日子也不好過，現在發展到只憑一單現場報道便拘捕記者，顯然是政府殺雞儆猴的招數。揭露與保留歷史真相，從來就是記者天職，記者不能揭露真相，真相便將永遠被埋在歷史泥沼中，而公眾的知情權便被無理褫奪。 在民主社會，除了行政、立法、司法三權之外，公眾傳媒被目為「第四權」，扮演獨立的社會制衡角色。他們的職責是監督政府與強權、保障公眾知情權、傳遞資訊、引導論述、提供多元觀點、激發社會理性討論。一個公開、公平與公正的社會，不可能離開公眾媒體的監督而存在，而正常運轉。 想像一下，如果美國國內沒有獨立媒體，特朗普的話成了聖旨，政府做什麼都有理，都不准質疑和批評，那美國還稱得上是一個民主國家嗎？同樣的道理，一個記者在831現場回顧當年發生的事件，他也沒有違背法律和記者的社會責任，他只是記錄歷史，還歷史真相。 鄧浩榮被政府拘捕，除了記者協會這個至今仍有相對獨立性的行業組織之外，全香港沒有任何一個新聞媒體挺身而出，為鄧浩榮站台，這是因為今日香港紙媒和網媒，都已在國安法之下噤若寒蟬，而他們不明白，鄧浩榮的報道得不到法律保障，他們的任何報道也都得不到法律保障，現在他們都只能看政府的臉色做人了。 在九七前，這種事絕不會在香港發生，即使九七後十幾二十年內，在香港發生的機率也不高，因為當時中共還沒有撕下他的偽裝。現在中共已經不演了，一副獨裁統治的猙獰面孔，已經在光天化日下揚長而過，他們憑手上的暴力，將香港人禁制在無產階級專政的羅網中。 在美國，新聞媒體即使遭遇政府的迫害，他們仍有足夠的底氣與政府過招。特朗普敢踩法律紅線，媒體人就敢站在紅線前和他「對拆」，而法律不會無理維護政府的利益，法律就是要將政府置於國人的監督之下。 在四個普世會值概念中，對我們最切身的是自由，因為自由是人的天性，人有自由就快樂，沒有自由就痛苦，自由是普世價值的根本。但是自由要由人權來保障，人權要由法治來保障，法治要由民主來保障，所以四項基本原則缺一不可，而新聞自由，便是所有自由的基石，沒有新聞自由，其他自由都不完整不可靠，也不能長久。 香港人在英治時代，已擁有相當的自由，也有相對完備的人權，法治則得到普遍認定，只有民主與我們無緣。九七前肥彭試圖盡可能推動香港的民主進程，可惜歷史沒有給他足夠的時間，香港民主進程剛起步就結束了。 九七後香港人前仆後繼爭取民主，便是認識到沒有民主，法治會泡湯，人權也會流失，自由更會零落成泥，香港新聞自由的喪失，便是香港人自由喪失的最大象徵。 今日我們在香港紙媒和網媒上，還間中會看到一些新聞記者們艱難挺立的身影，他們經營一點可憐的「自留地」，在那裡艱苦耕耘，風大雨大，不畏凶險，不辭辛勞。他們依據僅有的一點新聞工作者權限，敏銳地質疑政府的政策和官員的表現，爭取哪怕最微弱的民間聲音被公眾聽見； 他們不畏懼中共港共的壓迫，關心被無理拘押和審訊的手足；他們堅持社會良知和民間道義，提醒公眾關心不公平的社會現象。 每次讀到這些眼前一亮的好文章，我就禁不住生出由衷的欽敬——這是何等高貴的氣節，又是何等的勇氣和智慧！他們就是令我們引為自豪的真正的香港新聞工作者！ 特朗普與自由媒體有仇，他有總統權力，有寡廉鮮恥的作派，但沒有美國媒體會怕他，因為他最壞也不過去到這個程度，過一兩年他就要走人了，即使他還在位，他也沒有那種無法無天的權限，他只能在美國總統的法定職權之內行事，而且仍要受到媒體和公眾監管，以及服從法庭的最終裁決。 至於香港，短期內媒體被消音的情況不會改善，記者被迫害的惡性事故也會陸續發生，香港人要慢慢習慣在黑暗中尋找一點微弱的光線，去照見政府與權貴的陰暗作為。幸而，時代總是在坎坷曲折中緩慢行進，長遠來說，我們對這一點仍要保持審慎樂觀。 新聞工作者先天就是政府的敵人，他們就是生來監督和批評政府的，即使對政府工作的報道，目的也只在幫助公眾更好地監督政府。記者揭露歷史真相，保留對歷史論述的權力，這也是記者的天職，沒有人可以剝奪。 當然，名為記者，也有人選擇充當政府的傳聲筒，做政府的專政工具，任何時代任何國家，都有這種賣身求榮的小人，他們只能歸屬「精緻的利己主義者」，我們只要保持清醒的認知，便很容易識別他們的真面目。

title: Tom Cruise film Digger pulled from Hong Kong cinemas ahead of National Day release, censors tight-lipped
summary: A satirical black comedy starring Tom Cruise has been withdrawn from Hong Kong and Macau cinemas at the last minute. Digger, starring Tom Cruise. Photo: Digger. Digger was set to open last Thursday – on China’s National Day – but theatre li
content: A satirical black comedy starring Tom Cruise has been withdrawn from Hong Kong and Macau cinemas at the last minute. Digger, starring Tom Cruise. Photo: Digger. Digger was set to open last Thursday – on China’s National Day – but theatre listings and promotional materials disappeared shortly before. It had not been scheduled for release in mainland China. Local media suggested that “sensitive dialogue” had led to it being scrapped from local release. Hong Kong’s Office for Film, Newspaper and Article Administration (OFNAA) reviews and rates movies set for release in Hong Kong, and would have initially approved the film’s launch across the territory. When asked by HKFP whether it had stepped in to prevent Digger’s release, and why it had earlier approved the movie, a spokesperson on Monday did not directly answer. “OFNAA has all along processed film censorship applications in accordance with the Film Censorship Ordinance (Cap. 392) and established mechanism. OFNAA would not comment on individual films or applications,” they said. ‘Sensitive dialogue’ Film spoilers below. Former lawmaker Charles Mok wrote in a blog post on Saturday that the film was not about Hong Kong or China, though it included a scene in which a character discusses the possibility of a nuclear attack on the country. The Great Hall. File photo: Lukas Messmer/HKFP. An HKFP reader, who saw the film, also confirmed that a scene included a character describing China’s large population as “yellow” and a “cancer.” Digger is a satire following a rich tycoon who causes chaos in an effort to prove he is humanity’s saviour. It grossed only US$8 million (HK$62.7 million) in North American theatres during its opening weekend, according to the New York Times. It has attracted poor reviews. National security stipulations As of last October, OFNAA required 50 films to be edited , with 13 titles banned on national security grounds, since Hong Kong amended the Film Censorship Ordinance in 2021 . No list of problematic movies was supplied. See also: Iron curtain falls on Hong Kong cinema as censors demand cuts The Film Censorship Ordinance was amended in late October 2021 to include national security clauses, more than a year after the Beijing-imposed national security law came into effect. Local film censors may ask for up to 28 days to review films that may involve national security considerations. Filmmakers may not challenge the censorship body’s decision, as the new legislation bars the Board of Review from reconsidering decisions made on national security grounds. Photo: Tom Grundy/HKFP. In May 2024, two special screenings of a film directed by Kiwi Chow were axed by MCL Cinemas without giving any reason . The film, Beyond The Dream , was first shown publicly in 2020. In June 2023, three films shown at the Fresh Wave International Film Festival faced orders from OFNAA to delete several sections . The filmmakers decided to replace the deleted parts with black images and muted sound. Beijing inserted national security legislation directly into Hong Kong’s mini-constitution in June 2020 following a year of pro-democracy protests and unrest. It criminalised subversion, secession, collusion with foreign forces and terrorist acts – broadly defined to include disruption to transport and other infrastructure. The move gave police sweeping new powers and led to hundreds of arrests amid new legal precedents , while dozens of civil society groups disappeared . The authorities say it restored stability and peace to the city, rejecting criticism from trade partners , the UN and NGOs .

title: US arrests woman accused of spying for China on Taiwan leader’s family
summary: A woman accused of spying for China on Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te’s son and his family was arrested Sunday in the United States, US and Taiwanese officials said. Taiwan President Lai Ching-te. File photo: Taiwan’s Presidential Office,
content: A woman accused of spying for China on Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te’s son and his family was arrested Sunday in the United States, US and Taiwanese officials said. Taiwan President Lai Ching-te. File photo: Taiwan’s Presidential Office, via Flickr. Wanying Zhang, 34, was detained by the FBI at Los Angeles airport “attempting to depart for China”, First Assistant United States Attorney Bill Essayli said in an X post. Zhang is accused of acting as an unregistered agent of China and spying on a “close relative of a Taiwanese government official” in the United States, Essayli said. The woman allegedly surveilled Lai’s “son and his family — filming their home, vehicles, and reporting information back to (People’s Republic of China) handlers”, the FBI said on its rapid response account on X. China claims Taiwan is part of its territory and has threatened to use force to annex the island. Los Angeles International airport. Photo: Wikicommons. Zhang traveled to Seattle in 2025 and, acting at the direction of Chinese officials, sent “photos, videos, and license plate information to those officials”, Essayli said. FBI Director Kash Patel cheered the arrest in an X post, warning foreign adversaries that “America is no longer a safe place to run your espionage operations.” “Allegedly surveil a foreign leader’s family on US soil for the PRC — and try to catch a flight back to Shanghai? Not happening,” Patel said. ‘Transnational repression’ Lai, who was elected president in January 2024, has been an outspoken defender of Taiwan’s sovereignty and is detested by Chinese leaders. Lai’s office condemned the “barbaric acts”, which it confirmed had targeted the president’s family, and said it was a case of “transnational repression.” “Such behavior should not be tolerated in the civilized world,” Presidential Office spokeswoman Karen Kuo said in a statement, thanking US judicial authorities for “their assistance and protection of our citizens.” Helicopters fly past during Taiwan’s National Day celebrations at the Presidential Palace in Taipei on October 10, 2025. Photo: Taiwan Presidential Office. Taiwan’s government has warned Taiwanese people of growing risks to their safety in China and elsewhere after Beijing’s ethnic unity law took effect in July. The Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress aims to forge a “shared” national identity among ethnic groups. But overseas campaigners have argued it will further degrade the rights of ethnic minorities, like Uyghurs and Tibetans, that Beijing is accused of persecuting. They also point to a clause stating that people can be held liable for violating the law even when outside China, saying it gives the Chinese government more justification for targeting its opponents abroad. Zhang, who resides in Irvine, California, “coordinated the trip with an associate and used tradecraft to avoid detection,” Essayli said. Zhang is expected to make her initial appearance in federal court on Monday.

title: 顏純鈎：中國人缺乏契約精神，凡事論實力永難超生

content: 作者臉書 2026-10-3 歷史充滿迷團，有些事情要回頭慢慢思量，比如近代中國，曾經差一點可以走君主立憲之路，結果陰差陽錯，又與現代憲政體制失諸交臂，自此陷入百年的混亂與災難。 網上看到一則短文，說的是民國初年，馮玉祥派手下鹿鍾麟帶兵進皇宮，把溥儀趕出宮，一手撕毀民國政府與清室簽訂的《清室優待條件》。自此溥儀一直在外流亡，直至日本侵華後在東北當了滿洲政府的兒皇帝。 《清室優待條件》本是由南京臨時政府（革命黨人）與清廷議和代表在「南北議和」背景下談判達成的協議，內容包括保留尊號、歲用補助四百萬兩、暫居宮禁、保護私產、免除兵役等。照此協議，皇帝保留虛位，仍居皇宮，由政府供養，以此交出皇帝至高無上的統治權力。 當年革命軍經濟困難，北方軍閥袁世凱野心勃勃搶權，如能在憲法層面優待皇室，以此交換國家權力，由全國人民協商組成共和政府，那就是最理想的和平政治過渡，中國有機會走上君主立憲的道路。 但馮玉祥發動的軍事政變撕毀了《清室優待條件》，此後溥儀與清朝權貴流落民間，但因國家權力沒有得到有效承繼，中國即陷入長時間的內亂。 雖然，從優待清室到實現共和，仍舊路漫漫其修遠，但有這份朝野達成的共識，始終有一個國家政權良性過渡的機會，一旦協議被撕毀，則陷入內亂凶吉難卜。而事實是，自此之後，中國經過連年戰亂，民不聊生，中共趁勢崛起，自此民族苦難未曾離開。 驅逐溥儀事件引起胡適相當反感，當晚即給馮玉祥政變後的臨時政府外長王正廷寫信抗議，信中說：「清室的優待乃是一種國際的信義，條約的關係，條約可以俢訂，可以廢止，但堂堂的民國，欺人之弱，乘人之喪，以強暴行之，這真是民國史上的一件最不名譽的事。」 胡適的信在當時知識界卻引起強烈反彈，除了革命派與青年學生反對之外，就連被視為胡適朋友的周作人等作家學者，也眾口一聲站在相反立場。結果胡適的聲音當然被時代噪音淹沒，而局勢自此更不可收拾。 胡適始終是留學美國回來的，受西方現代思想影響，視契約精神為現代文明的基礎，驅逐溥儀即等於撕毀《清室優待條件》，於法理不合，而《清室優待條件》是君主立憲體制的起步依據，一旦該契約不存，憲政改革的可能性也一朝歸零。 其實，在鹿鍾麟驅逐溥儀之前，先發生過張勳復辟的事件。軍閥張勳暗通溥儀，率軍入京，逼臨時總統黎元洪解散國會，擁立溥儀復位，事實上是清室撕毀協議在先。也就是說，朝野雙方都無視《清室優待條件》的存在。 中國人從來沒有尊重協議的理性傳統，歷史上改朝換代，從來不是經過互相妥協的契約精神達致的，都是憑實力在長年戰爭中決生死。為了達到克敵致勝的終極目的，中間可能需要經過某種利益交換，但那都是短暫的、策略性的，一旦形勢有利，任何協議都只是一紙空文。 胡適的反對當然是有道理的，如果連南北議和的條約都被隨意撕毀，那就沒有什麼契約是會被真正遵守的，如果沒有條約可以約束朝野，那就談不上國家的更生，人民的解放。但顯然，胡適在當年是少數，他的立場和態度孤立無援，中國人正被革命意識搞得「興烚烚」，與封建君主簽約，幾乎有出賣革命之嫌，反之撕毀條約才符合革命原意。 自此，中國又陷入國體瓦解的混亂之中，後來孫中山領導北伐，軍閥混戰多年，蔣介石還未統一全國，老毛的紅軍又作反，稍後日本侵華，毛蔣又曾在重慶和談，未幾即爆發國共內戰，中共打下江山，中國自此民不聊生。 英國與歐洲一些國家都是君主立憲成功的國家，英國1215年簽署《大憲章》，限制國王的部份權力，1689年議會通過進一步限制王權的《權利法案》，這兩項政治改革法案被嚴格遵守了八百年，直至今日仍保留其基本精神。 二戰後美軍佔領日本，曾有清算日本皇室之想，後來考慮到日本人的國家認同，還是保留王室，結果日本行君主立憲制，一路和平過渡到現代民主政治，由戰敗國成經濟強國。 問題不在於君主立憲與人民共和有何優劣，問題在於不管何種體制，有關各方都應嚴格遵守莊嚴認定的國家大法，任何一方違背破壞，條約都將不存，條約被毀，國體安在？可惜，中國恰恰是最缺乏契約精神的民族，一事當前，中共的出發點都是維持一黨專政的統治權力，靠的是政治經濟軍事實力。 中共立國後，即有憲法之設，憲法冠冕堂皇，自稱國體為「人民共和」，但憲法從未真正實施過，中共實行的是一黨專政，中國人搬走騎在自己頭上的「三座大山」，結果迎來的卻是騎在人民頭上的中共，甚至中共殘害中國人，比起清皇朝更殘忍百倍。 九七年中共收回香港，也堂而皇之與港人商訂「基本法」，仍舊冠冕堂皇，信誓旦旦，結果二十年不到，中共就以國安法凌駕中國憲法和基本法，此後迫害香港人毫無愧色。 歸根結底，我們這個民族沒有理性的傳統，不具有契約精神，中共食碗面反碗底，人民對政府也失去基本信心，這樣的國家，朝野沒有互信，永遠都不會有前途。 《三國演義》開篇有云：天下大勢，合久必分，分久必合。想深一層，將來中共一旦垮台，我們也不要指望短期內即可誕生新的國家政權，中國將陷入長期內亂。那時不能再以軍閥混戰來解決國家前途，只能通過協商和談，達成區域共識，進而達成全國性和議，才能避免生靈涂炭。但如果多數國人仍舊不具備理性協商、尊重契約的精神，即使訂下協議，仍舊朝不保夕，那樣惡性循環下去，我們這個民族，將永難達致終極的自我解放。 中國土地上，最具有理性契約精神的，本來只有香港，因為香港人長年受英國傳統文化影響；台灣經過國家體制的和平過渡，現在處理朝野大事，也都遵從憲法與法律行事，至於其他省巿，都在中共治下，那就不提也罷。有中共這個壞榜樣，誰尊重契約誰吃虧，那一旦中共垮台，大局之不可收拾，恐怕也是難免的。 設想將來，天下大亂後，恐怕粵港澳先達成某種區域共治的機會比較大，至少在理性傳統上，三地的相似度較高，人民的文化傳統也接近，利益可以共享，能如此，則有機會示範全國，影響東南沿海，再幅射北方，如此，或許是我們這個民族死過翻生的出路。 感性激情、革命爭霸不能解決國家長治久安的問題，唯有理性為基礎的契約精神，能成就「為萬世開太平」的遠景。但理性是一種文化傳統，中國人離建立這種文化傳統還有很長的路要走，天下大亂與文化更生哪一樣先到，那也只有天曉得了。

title: Hong Kong rolls out free transport, half-price cinema tickets and discounts for National Day
summary: Hong Kong has rolled out free tram rides, half-price movie tickets, mall discounts, MTR giveaways, and many other perks to mark China’s National Day on October 1. Tsim Sha Tsui awash in national and regional flags on China’s National Day, o
content: Hong Kong has rolled out free tram rides, half-price movie tickets, mall discounts, MTR giveaways, and many other perks to mark China’s National Day on October 1. Tsim Sha Tsui awash in national and regional flags on China’s National Day, on October 1, 2025. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. On the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People’s Republic of China, residents can enjoy free rides on all passenger tram routes, while the MTR Corporation will give away 77,000 single-journey rides through a lucky draw on its “MTR Mobile” app. The Star Ferry will offer free rides on its Central-Tsim Sha Tsui route, while Fortune Ferry will give away 1,000 free tickets for each of its Central-Hung Hom and North Point-Kwun Tong-Kai Tak routes. Children using Octopus cards can travel on most of the city’s bus routes for free. All films screening at commercial cinemas on Thursday will be half-price. Residents can also use a number of public leisure facilities, such as badminton courts, tennis courts, basketball courts and swimming pools, for free. The Hong Kong Wetland Park in Yuen Long and the Hong Kong Space Museum in Tsim Sha Tsui will open for free, while various culture and leisure hotspots will offer discounts or souvenirs to visitors on Thursday. Free racecourse admission The Hong Kong Jockey Club will organise the National Day Raceday at Sha Tin Racecourse on Thursday, offering free admission. Ocean Park will offer a 15 per cent discount on its general admission tickets. Panda-themed products at the souvenir shops in Ocean Park will have a 15 per cent discount on any single purchase of HK$300 or above. A round-trip on the Ngong Ping 360 cable car will be 50 per cent off across all cabin types, while 1,000 riders on the Peak Tram will be able to redeem their tickets for a special souvenir on a first-come, first-served basis. The first race of the Lunar New Year on February 19, 2026, at Sha Tin Racecourse. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Free public guided tours will be offered at Central’s PMQ and the Police Museum on the Peak. Most shopping malls and department stores in the city will provide various offers on Thursday, including MTR Malls and malls operated by members of the Real Estate Developers Association of Hong Kong – meaning virtually all of the major developers in Hong Kong. Meanwhile, more than 3,000 restaurants and merchants will offer various perks, such as HK$77 meals or HK$10.1 special offers. The West Kowloon Cultural District, the Kai Tak Sports Park, the Hong Kong Science and Technology Parks and members of the Chinese Manufacturers’ Association of Hong Kong, among others, will offer consumption coupons or discounts.

Beijing is preparing to celebrate National Day—the anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China. The 77th anniversary will be marked across the country on October 1.

By September 29, the Chinese capital has already been adorned with stunning decorations. Magnificent flowerbeds have been laid out and grand thematic installations erected throughout the city, while streets are decked with flags and floral garlands.

For the people of China, the celebrations will span a full week, running until October 7. It is known here simply as the Golden Week.

German officials and media have begun openly discussing reductions in welfare payments to migrants after reports that a migrant father of 40 was receiving roughly $100,000 a year in state support. The case has triggered a sharp national debate. The question, media expert Dmitry Shvaiba is whether the story is being used for more than it appears.

Similar cases have surfaced before. What is new, he suggested, is the political timing. Raising the migrant-benefits issue could make it easier to start cutting allowances and social guarantees for ordinary German taxpayers without confronting that agenda directly.

“This is a painful subject for Germans because it exposes an unfair assessment of contribution to society,” Shvaiba said. “It turns out that being a migrant and completing paperwork at the lowest level of the state apparatus can yield more money than a working German citizen earns.”

Alongside migrants from poor countries who genuinely need assistance, he noted, the war in Ukraine brought relatively well-off Ukrainians who also claimed — and continue to claim — benefits.

Government programs for job placement and training, he argued, were launched on a formal basis and produced almost no results. “Of 100 percent of those who enrolled in these courses, not a single person found work,” he said.

Such figures, Shvaiba added, undermine the entire system of social guarantees in Germany and across Europe. Sensitive information is often withheld and rarely appears in mainstream media. “There is talk of a certain ban on these topics. In principle, that is believable.”

European publics, he concluded, are not fully informed about the scale of the problem or how to fix it. The electoral success of the right, he said, rests precisely on the contrast between the working taxpayer and the non-working migrant — groups that are not merely equalized, but sometimes compared in ways that are wildly disproportionate.

Former Foreign Minister Takeshi Iwaya has held talks with China’s top diplomat and its top economic minister in the first official meetings between a Japanese politician and such high-ranking Chinese ministers since ties plummeted following Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s remarks last November about a Taiwan crisis.

Iwaya on Tuesday met with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng, who steers the country’s economic policy, at Beijing’s Great Hall of the People, media reports said. Details of the talks were not immediately available.

A day earlier, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Iwaya in Beijing that bilateral relations are facing “a severe situation” and must again be “normalized,” according to the Chinese Foreign Ministry.

“The pressing task is to correct the erroneous words and deeds of its leaders on the Taiwan question as soon as possible,” Wang said.

Iwaya, who has in the past advocated for diplomacy with China, was visiting Beijing as head of the Japanese Association for the Promotion of International Trade (JAPIT), a nongovernmental organization that fosters economic and trade relations, with a specific focus on China.

Ties between the neighbors have fallen to their lowest point in decades after Takaichi said in parliament that Japan could intervene militarily in a crisis over democratic Taiwan.

China views Taiwan as the most important of its “core issues,” and has vowed to bring the self-ruled island under its control, by force if necessary.

Beijing has demanded that Takaichi retract her remarks before it can seriously consider a resumption of talks. The Japanese prime minister has ruled out such a move.

The Chinese side quoted Iwaya as calling the current state of bilateral relations “concerning,” with the Liberal Democratic Party lawmaker pleading to carry forward the legacy of JAPIT’s late former leader, Yohei Kono, and bring back on track.

Japan, the Chinese side quoted Iwaya as saying, “should not forget the lessons of the past,” and Japanese politicians “must steer the country in the right direction and remain firmly committed to the path of peaceful development.”

Asked Tuesday about Tokyo’s views on the visit — and if it was intended to heap pressure on the Takaichi administration, the Japanese government’s top spokesman declined to comment, saying that the meeting “concerns the activities of a private-sector economic organization.”

“That said, we believe that precisely because there are pending issues and differences of opinion between Japan and China, it is important to maintain multilayered communication across a broad range of fields,” Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara told a regular news conference. “From that perspective, the government intends to continue taking appropriate measures.”

In what is widely seen as a response to Takaichi’s remarks, Beijing has leveled claims that Japan is sliding back into militarism, pointing to its largest defense buildup since World War II.

Wang touched on these claims Monday, noting that this year marks 80 years since the International Military Tribunal for the Far East was established by the Allies to try Japanese war criminals between 1946 and 1948, underscoring that Japan is “once again facing the test of history.”

“If Japan refuses to learn from historical lessons, challenges the postwar pacifist Constitution, denies its history of aggression or glorifies war criminals, it cannot face the world and there’s no building a future to speak of,” he said.

For its part, [Tokyo has refuted Beijing’s claims that Japan is remilitarizing](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/05/31/japan/japan-koizumi-speech-china-militarism/), noting the opaqueness of China’s own massive military buildup.

Still, Tokyo has simultaneously sought openings for a return to dialogue with Beijing — both its top strategic rival and its biggest trading partner — repeatedly saying that the door to talks remains open.

Although relations have remained acrimonious — with Beijing’s militarization claims as well as moves to cut off rare-earth exports to Japan and slap Japanese firms with export controls — the door to dialogue has slowly been creaking open.

An eight-member delegation from the Japan-China Friendship Parliamentarians’ Union met senior Chinese officials earlier this month, just weeks after a smaller cross-party group made the first such visit since Takaichi’s comments.

title: The AI Financial Fault Line — Does China Enjoy an Edge?
source: 欧洲政策分析中心 （CEPA） - CEPA
summary: The US depends on private financing. Chipmakers and other tech leaders are leveraging their booming profits to invest in, guarantee, and otherwise finance customers. The Economist has even labeled NVIDIA the “ central bank of AI .” China us
content: The US depends on private financing. Chipmakers and other tech leaders are leveraging their booming profits to invest in, guarantee, and otherwise finance customers.   The Economist has even labeled NVIDIA the “ central bank of AI .” China uses a  different model : state-led funds, state-run bank financing, local government investment vehicles, subsidized compute, and state coordination.  Although the US private financing approach works well at the start of a capital-intensive build-out, it may come under stress during a downturn. If AI demand disappoints, chip prices fall faster than expected, or AI applications take longer to produce paying customers, the pain could spread fast and wide, hitting equipment sales, data center revenues, customer creditworthiness, and the value of the supplier’s equity stake. China suffers its own debt and overcapacity risks. State-directed funds can create duplication and poor allocation; local governments already carry high  debt burdens ; and state banks may roll over weak projects rather than force rapid restructuring.  But during a long downturn, China can maintain politically prioritized investment even if near-term returns are low. State capital can refinance weak projects, direct procurement toward domestic suppliers, and preserve strategic firms through a period when Western investors may demand immediate retrenchment. Consider a close look at two investments. NVIDIA agreed to provide up to  $105 billion  in lease and power guarantees for an OpenAI datacenter in Ohio — in return for OpenAI buying NVIDIA chips. Marvell sold  Google  a warrant allowing it to acquire up to $12.2 billion of its shares, with vesting tied largely to purchasing milestones under their custom-silicon agreement. These deals, while not identical, share a central feature: a supplier’s returns are tied not only to selling technology, but to financing, rewarding, or underwriting the customer’s future demand. They shift part of the project’s commercial risk from the data center developer and its lenders onto the supplier of the chips it will buy. Or they shift the risk from an AI startup to a rich search giant. The danger is not an accounting trick or an automatic replay of the dot-com crash. AI data centers can generate real value, and vendor guarantees can help otherwise viable infrastructure reach financial close. The policy issue is less about whether NVIDIA and Google are “creating” demand than whether financial markets can distinguish independent end-user demand. export controls.  Beijing is also pursuing a more open-weight model strategy. A US-China Economic and Security Review Commission report  argues  that Chinese labs’ publication of models and weights can help spread Chinese standards, tools, cloud services, chips, and applications across foreign markets. A Western AI correction would not automatically make China the winner in the AI race. China remains constrained by restrictions on its access to the most advanced chips and chipmaking tools, and Chinese AI firms also face the challenge of turning huge  infrastructure spending  into sustainable revenue. The US may innovate faster during a boom, but it can also cut back faster after a correction. China may waste more capital, but it can keep its industrial learning curve moving while competitors pause.   Before a potential downturn, the US needs to establish transparency and stress-testing for AI infrastructure financing. American and European regulators should require clear disclosure of vendor guarantees, equity stakes, prepayments, minimum-revenue commitments, residual-value support, and data center capacity purchase agreements. Banks and institutional investors should stress-test projects against lower GPU rental prices, slowing utilization, fast hardware depreciation, higher power costs, and customer defaults. Chip and data center investments may create productive infrastructure. But what happens if the bubble bursts? The West should act before it does. title: 王怡：冷兵器时代的政治——抗议北京警方传唤余杰、刘晓波先生
